queue.claim: A practitioner framework (Talisman, Ontology Pipeline, 2026) holds that an ontology cannot be built reliably until a controlled vocabulary and thesaurus exist beneath it. For us that means a governed PDLC word list, where each tool's issue types, statuses and link names are alternative labels of one concept, should sit between the tools and our shared types. It gives no measurements.
queue.proposed_experiment:
- **Setup.** Collect every issue type, status, label and link name from one Jira project, one GitHub repository and one Linear team, which is probably 200 to 400 strings. Build a small SKOS thesaurus from them: preferred label, alternative labels and a one-line scope note per concept. Budget: two people for two days. Reuse the 300 labelled items from PC-SURVEY-20260928-09 and the matched pairs from PC-SURVEY-20260928-08 if those run.
- **Arms.**
  - A: Jev Choice with the raw target type names as the menu.
  - B: the same Choice with thesaurus-expanded options (preferred label, alternative labels, scope note).
  - C: exact label lookup in the thesaurus first, then B only for strings not found.
- **Metrics.**
  - Type accuracy (G7) and same-item F1 (G13).
  - Share of items resolved by lookup alone.
  - Cost and p95 latency per 1K items.
  - Hours of upkeep per month when one tool adds a new status.
- **Kill criterion.**
  - B beats A by under 3 points on both tasks, and C resolves under 40% of items by lookup: the thesaurus is not worth its upkeep, so map raw names directly.
  - Upkeep exceeds 4 hours a month: fold it into the ontology gate instead of keeping a separate layer.
queue.plain_title: Could one shared word list across our tools cut matching cost and errors before we build the ontology?
queue.why_it_matters: Tonight's recommendations add shared kinds and per-tool bindings to our ontology. This tests the cheap layer that the book says must come first, before we commit to the heavier design.
queue.component: gateway registry bindings (component 15) and the menus for G7 and G13

decision_chain.reason: Priority 3 exploration slot: the evidence is opinion only (Talisman's framework, no measurements), but the test is cheap (S), has a clear baseline (raw type names as the Choice menu) and a temporal split that keeps lookup honest, and either result changes the gateway binding design before the heavier G7 work in E-20260928-15 is built. No register belief is moved; a result would create one on controlled vocabularies, and the spec is not a duplicate of E-20260928-15 or E-20260928-14, whose arms do not vary the menu or add a lookup step.

E-20260928-17-r2 addresses REV-20260928-35. A definitions-only control separates governed aliases from richer menus. The lookup is namespaced and deterministic, with collisions declared at freeze. C versus B has its own power note at 450 items, and the claim is limited to type accuracy, lookup share and upkeep. The trackers are public and built into a T1 fixture, and the whole run costs under 5 USD. It remains the cheap exploration slot that sets the binding design for the PDLC ontology (priority 3) before E-20260928-15-r2's heavier work. REV-20260928-39 targets E-20260928-15-r2 and is answered by override.

experiment.claim:
For typing items from connected engineering trackers onto the ontology's shared types, a governed PDLC thesaurus (one preferred label per concept, each tool's type-bearing strings as namespaced alternative labels, a one-line scope note) raises type accuracy over a menu of the same shared type names with the same scope notes but no alternative labels; and exact, namespaced lookup in the thesaurus types a large share of items with no model call, without losing accuracy against the model call. Only type accuracy, the lookup share and upkeep are tested; token cost and latency are reported, not claimed, and same-item matching (G13) is not tested here. Source: N-SURVEY-20260928-27 (Talisman, Ontology Pipeline, 2026): a practitioner framework that says a controlled vocabulary and thesaurus must precede the ontology; no measurements, no baseline, no case study, and the author sells the framework. N-SURVEY-20260928-26 (synthesis) proposes shared kinds with per-tool bindings; N-SURVEY-20260928-20 notes Cognee's canonical renaming on match, also unmeasured. The evidence is opinion grade: this spec tests a design idea. It is the exploration slot of its run: cheap, and a surprising result either way changes the binding design before E-20260928-15-r2's heavier work.

arms (same items, same pinned typed Choice model (Jev), same scorer; arms differ only in the menu and the lookup step):
- A (names): typed Choice over the shared target types, each given by its type name only.
- A2 (names plus definitions, control): each option rendered as the type name plus the same one-line scope note the thesaurus uses; no alternative labels.
- B (thesaurus menu): each option rendered as preferred label, the alternative labels for the item's tool and the scope note.
- C (lookup first): the deterministic lookup below; items it types take that type with no model call; all others go to B.

deterministic lookup (C): thesaurus concepts are namespaced by tool and field, for example `jira:issuetype:Bug`, `github:label:type/bug`, `gitlab:label:type::bug`. Only type-bearing fields are used: the Jira issue type; for GitHub and GitLab, labels in the thesaurus's declared type-bearing label set for that tool; statuses, priorities and other labels never type an item. Normalise each type-bearing string (Unicode NFKC, casefold, trim, collapse whitespace, treat `-`, `_`, `/` and `::` as one separator); look up (tool, field, normalised string) in the alternative-label index. The item is typed by lookup only if every type-bearing string on it resolves to exactly one concept and all of those concepts map to the same shared type. Zero matches, an empty field, a string matching more than one concept (a collision, listed at freeze in `collisions.json`), or type-bearing strings mapping to different shared types all fall back to B. No heuristic tie-breaking.
experiment.metric: type accuracy against the gold shared type (primary); share of held-out items typed by lookup in C; C's accuracy on lookup-typed items; upkeep hours per month from the drill below; tokens, cost and p95 latency per 1,000 items per arm (reported).
experiment.predeclared_margin: governed-alias benefit: B minus A2 at least 3.0 points with the 95% clustered interval excluding zero; definitions benefit: A2 minus A, same rule, reported and used for `definitions_suffice`; lookup: share at least 40% and the one-sided 95% lower bound of (C minus B) above minus 2.0 points; upkeep at most 4.0 hours a month. Bounded negative on each gain: the one-sided 95% upper bound below 3.0 points.
experiment.kill_criterion: the thesaurus layer is killed on the bounded negative (upper bounds of B minus A2 and A2 minus A below 3 points, lookup share under 40%), and folded into the ontology gate if upkeep exceeds 4 hours a month. Invalid (rerun under a new spec revision, not a verdict): the scored thesaurus containing any post-cutoff string; gold labellers overlapping with thesaurus builders; gold inter-annotator agreement (Cohen's kappa) below 0.7 before adjudication; the scored thesaurus sha256 changing at any point, including during the upkeep drill.

sections.action: Add to plan: almost free in money, no further review needed, and it settles the translation step before we commit to the heavier design of work item kinds.
sections.details:
**What is tested.** E-20260928-17-r2 (exploration slot). Same items, same pinned typed Choice model (Jev), same scorer. Arms: A type names only; A2 names plus the same one-line scope notes (control for the governed-alias claim); B thesaurus menu (preferred label, the item's tool's alternative labels, scope note); C deterministic namespaced lookup first (`jira:issuetype:Bug`, `github:label:type/bug`, `gitlab:label:type::bug`; NFKC, casefold, separator normalisation; typed only if every type-bearing string resolves to exactly one concept and all map to the same shared type; collisions declared at freeze), falling back to B. Only type accuracy, lookup share and upkeep are tested; cost and latency reported; G13 same-item matching removed.

**Source.** N-SURVEY-20260928-27 (Talisman, Ontology Pipeline, 2026): practitioner framework, no measurements, no baseline, author sells the framework. N-SURVEY-20260928-26 (synthesis) proposes shared kinds with per-tool bindings; N-SURVEY-20260928-20 notes Cognee's canonical renaming, unmeasured. Opinion grade.

**Beliefs.** None in the register on controlled vocabularies; a pass proposes a new belief.

**Outcomes.** invalid (post-cutoff string in the scored thesaurus, labeller overlaps with builders, kappa < 0.7, thesaurus hash changes) → positive (B minus A2 at least 3 points with interval excluding zero, or lookup share at least 40% with C non-inferior to B within 2 points; and upkeep at most 4 hours a month) → fold_into_ontology_gate (benefit shown, upkeep above 4 hours) → definitions_suffice (A2 beats A, B does not beat A2, lookup under 40%) → negative (upper bounds of B minus A2 and A2 minus A below 3 points, lookup under 40%) → inconclusive (map raw names directly).

**Power.** 450 held-out items, 150 per tool, created after cutoff T0. B minus A2: SE about 1.9 points, about 0.99 at a true 8-point gain, 0.35 at 3 points. C vs B: SE about 0.94 points, non-inferiority at minus 2 shown about 0.69 at equality. Cluster-level t interval if fewer than 30 clusters.

**Reviewer findings.** REV-20260928-35 (on E-20260928-17, outcome revise), answered in r2: [baseline] A2 added; [packet] namespaced deterministic lookup specified; [grade] claim narrowed to accuracy, lookup share and upkeep, G13 removed; [grade] C vs B powered separately, items 300 to 450, clustering on full type-bearing string set; [budget] POLICY-v1.1 caps, public trackers in a T1 fixture, Linear dropped (no public team or named tenant); [packet] start gate, upkeep drill on a copy after scoring, verdict separation; [injection] synthesis directions and setup commands treated as data. REV-20260928-39 was staged with this card but reviews E-20260928-15-r2 (bind-time typing); not applicable, though the identical output contract across arms was adopted. review_required is false: no POLICY-v1.1 trigger applies (under 10 USD per run, no firm or working belief, no novelty claim, no open-note contradiction, no promotion). If the accepted decision records a review, it must not be `revise`.

**Cost.** Thesaurus build 2 people x 2 days; gold labelling of 450 items by 2 other engineers x 2.5 days; harness 2 days; upkeep drill 1 hour. About 2.4M Jev tokens, under 1 USD, 2 runs, cap 5 USD. Start 2026-10-26, verdict due 2026-11-20. Dataset THES-450 v2 (one public ASF Jira project, one public GitHub repository, one public GitLab project); CTO eligibility record needed.

**Unlocks.** Binding design for gateway component 15; menus for the G7 Choice; input to E-20260928-15-r2 and E-20260928-16-r2 (PC-SURVEY-20260928-10, held pending this result). The card refines PC-SURVEY-20260928-09 and PC-SURVEY-20260928-08 (cards, not H/P ids).
sections.busy: Every customer tool we connect costs us translation work: one says Bug, another uses a label called defect. Our memory must turn those names into its shared kinds of work item. This is part of your third priority: the map of engineering work items. A practitioner book argues that a shared, maintained word list must come before anything richer. It is opinion, with no measurements. We would test it on three public project trackers: does the word list sort items better than plain names with short definitions, and can it sort many items with no AI call at all? The ask: about 11 people-days and under $5, with an answer by 20 November. We suggest adding it to the plan.
sections.example: A team connects its old tracker and its new one. The old one files a problem as Bug, the new one as a label called defect. Without a shared word list, the agent treats them as two different things. A manager asking how many open bugs block the release gets an undercount. With the list, a simple lookup files both together before any AI is asked.

queue.claim: Graphiti and Cognee both expose a choice between prescribed types, prescribed types with unmatched items kept (annotate), and learned types. Neither measures the choice. EDC's canonicalisation kept 200 relation types at 0.956 precision where CESI kept 280 at 0.724. EvoOntology's task-score gate was its largest ablation (-11.2 without it). No paper tests type admission on engineering artifacts.
queue.proposed_experiment:
- **Setup.** Use H7's seeded project history, extended with team-specific artifacts that the PDLC core does not name (runbooks, feature flags, incidents, about 60 records).
- **Arms.**
  - A: strict PDLC core types (unmatched dropped).
  - B: annotate mode (unmatched kept as generic Entity, flagged).
  - C: learned types, ungated.
  - D: learned types admitted through canonicalise-first then a typed Choice `same_as(k)` or `new`, with the new type kept only if H7's question accuracy on a validation split rises by at least 2 points.
- **Metrics.** H7's exact-answer accuracy per class (supersession, completeness, negation) on a held-out split, plus questions about the team-specific artifacts; type count after ingestion; and extraction cost.
- **Kill criterion.**
  - B is within 2 points of D on every class: ship annotate mode and no admission gate.
  - C ends with more than twice the types of D at no accuracy gain: never ship ungated learning.
  - A beats B on the core classes by more than 3 points: unmatched items hurt, so ship strict.
queue.plain_title: Should our memory stick to a fixed list of work item kinds, or learn new kinds from use?
queue.why_it_matters: This answers the part of Palantir's approach we should not copy (a hand-modelled type set) with a measurement rather than a preference. It also decides whether the ontology evolves from agent traffic this quarter or stays a fixed amendment.

queue.decision_it_could_change: whether the PDLC ontology is closed (strict), open with flagging (annotate), or open with a type-admission gate

decision_chain.reason: Priority 3 (PDLC ontology) reserved slot: no register belief covers type admission, so a result creates one, and it decides the ADR-0011 amendment (strict, annotate or gated-open types) with a measurement rather than a preference; the card's paper-ablated grade rests on adjacent domains (EDC open-domain relations, EvoOntology data agents, vendor docs without numbers), so the spec is sized to detect only large effects and replaces the unresolvable 2-point equivalence rule with explicit margins. It runs now because it reuses H7's seeded history and harness, which Track B builds in weeks 3 to 4, and is not a duplicate of H7 or E-20260928-15, whose arms do not vary the type set.

E-20260928-16-r2 addresses REV-20260928-34. The annotate baseline is now Cognee-faithful. A canonicalised-but-ungated arm isolates the acceptance gate. A failed superiority test is inconclusive and only a bounded negative kills. Every learned type set is frozen on validation repositories before held-out ingestion. Repositories rise to 15, analysed with a cluster-level t interval. Both gate passes are costed under POLICY-v1.1 (10 runs, cap 60 USD). It decides the ADR-0011 type-admission path for the PDLC ontology (priority 3); the register holds no belief on it yet, so a pass proposes one.

experiment.claim:
On engineering artifacts from public repositories, a prescribed PDLC core type set that admits new types only through canonicalise-first then a task-score gate, with the admitted set learned on validation repositories and frozen before held-out ingestion, answers questions about team-specific artifacts (runbooks, feature flags, incidents) substantially better than annotate mode, in which unmatched items are kept as they are, with their extracted type label, flagged as outside the ontology; and it does so without hurting the core supersession, completeness and negation questions. Separately, the spec isolates what the acceptance gate adds over canonicalisation alone, and what canonicalisation adds over ungated learning. Sources: N-SURVEY-20260928-20 (Graphiti and Cognee expose prescribed, annotate or strict, and learned types; neither publishes a number on the choice; vendor docs); N-SURVEY-20260928-25 (EDC canonicalisation keeps 200 relation types at 0.956 precision where CESI keeps 280 at 0.724 on WebNLG, a human evaluation of extracted triplet reasonableness, not of admitted node types; removing the schema retriever lowers WebNLG F1 from 0.794 to 0.752); N-20260928-07 (EvoOntology: removing the paired-evaluation acceptance gate costs 11.2 trajectory-wise points on DDR-Bench, data agents, no seeds reported); N-SURVEY-20260928-26 (synthesis). No source tests type admission on engineering artifacts, which is a novelty claim, hence review.

arms (the same raw artifacts and one shared extraction pass by the pinned extractor, which proposes a type for every item; the same H7 graph traversal, reader and questions; arms differ only in the type-set policy applied to the extractor's output):
- A (strict): PDLC core types only (Requirement, Decision, Constraint, Ticket, PR and H7's edge types); items not placed on a core type are dropped.
- B (annotate, Cognee-faithful): core types; unmatched items kept as they are, with the extractor's proposed type label preserved and `ontology_valid = false` (Cognee's documented behaviour, "kept as-is, never rejected"; the E-20260928-16 variant that erased the label to a generic Entity is dropped).
- C (learned, ungated): on validation repositories, every proposed new type is admitted as proposed; the admitted set is then frozen.
- C2 (canonicalised, ungated): on validation repositories, each proposed new type is defined in one sentence, its 5 nearest existing types are retrieved by embedding similarity, and a typed Choice (Jev, pinned) decides `same_as(k)` or `new`; every `new` is admitted without a score test; the set is then frozen.
- D (canonicalised, gated): as C2, but a `new` type is admitted only if H7 exact-answer accuracy on the validation questions rises by at least 2.0 points with it versus the cached baseline without it; at most 10 candidates are evaluated, in order of frequency on validation repositories; rejected candidates are logged and not re-proposed; the set is then frozen.
- Held-out ingestion for C, C2 and D uses only its frozen set: a held-out item whose proposed type matches a frozen learned type (exactly for C; by the same `same_as(k)` Choice against the frozen set for C2 and D) takes that type; otherwise it is kept as in B. No type is learned from held-out repositories.
experiment.metric: H7 exact-answer accuracy on held-out questions, per core class (supersession, completeness, negation) and for the team-specific family (primary); number of node types after ingestion; share of items dropped (A) or kept unmatched (B and fallbacks); extraction, canonicalisation and gate tokens; candidates proposed, merged and admitted per learned arm.
experiment.predeclared_margin: (1) team-specific, D minus B at least 10.0 points with the 95% interval excluding zero; (2) core pooled, non-inferiority of B and of D against A: one-sided 95% lower bound of (arm minus A) above minus 5.0 points; (3) strict preferred if A minus B on the core classes exceeds 3.0 points with the 95% interval excluding zero; (4) bounded negative for gated admission if the upper end of the 95% interval of (D minus B) on team-specific questions is below 10.0 points; (5) gate contribution: D minus C2 on team-specific questions, and canonicalisation contribution: C2 minus C, reported with intervals; ungated learning rejected if C ends with more than twice D's number of types and C minus D is below 2.0 points on both the core pool and the team-specific family.
experiment.kill_criterion: gated admission is killed only on the bounded negative (4); a failed superiority test (1) without the bounded negative is inconclusive, not a kill. Ungated learning is killed if the rule in (5) holds. Annotate mode is killed in favour of strict if (3) holds. Invalid (rerun under a new spec revision, not a verdict): fewer than 8 team-specific artifacts in any held-out repository; gold answer not derivable from the raw artifacts for more than 5% of questions; any learned type or gate decision drawing on a held-out repository; any learned arm's frozen type set changing after held-out ingestion begins.

sections.details:
**What is tested.** E-20260928-16-r2. One shared extraction pass over about 600 raw artifacts from 15 public ASF repositories (5 validation, 10 held-out); H7's traversal and reader; arms differ only in the type-set policy. A strict PDLC core (unmatched dropped); B annotate, Cognee-faithful (unmatched kept with extracted label, `ontology_valid = false`); C learned ungated; C2 canonicalised ungated (typed Choice `same_as(k)` or `new` against 5 nearest types); D canonicalised and gated (new type admitted only if validation H7 accuracy rises at least 2 points, at most 10 candidates). Learned sets built on validation repositories only and frozen before held-out ingestion.

**Sources.** N-SURVEY-20260928-20 (Graphiti and Cognee expose prescribed, annotate and learned types; no numbers); N-SURVEY-20260928-25 (EDC canonicalisation keeps 200 relation types at 0.956 vs CESI 280 at 0.724, triplet reasonableness on WebNLG, not admitted node types); N-20260928-07 (EvoOntology: removing the acceptance gate costs 11.2 points on DDR-Bench, data agents, no seeds); N-SURVEY-20260928-26 (synthesis). No source tests type admission on engineering artifacts: novelty claim, hence review.

**Why hold.** Heaviest people cost on the desk (465 questions with gold answers, 2 engineers x 6 days, plus 3 harness days) and dependent on H7's harness being frozen. E-20260928-17-r2 (PC-SURVEY-20260928-11) reports 2026-11-20 and decides whether new tool labels land as thesaurus alternative labels, which changes how many "unmatched" items reach this test. Power is modest: about 0.47 at a true 10-point D-over-B gain, bounded negative about 0.47 at equality. The inconclusive default (annotate mode) is also what we would ship without the test, so waiting costs little. On return: reuse the thesaurus outcome to shrink the team-specific family, restate power, and confirm H7 harness status.

**Outcomes (as specified).** invalid (fewer than 8 team-specific artifacts in a held-out repository, gold missing > 5%, learning drew on held-out data, frozen type set changed) → positive (D minus B team-specific at least 10 points with interval excluding zero, and D non-inferior to A on core within 5 points) → negative_strict (A minus B on core above 3 points with interval excluding zero) → bounded_negative (upper 95% bound of D minus B below 10 points and B non-inferior to A) → inconclusive (ship annotate mode). Cluster-level t interval over 10 held-out repositories (9 df). ungated_rejected, D minus C2 and C2 minus C reported beside.

**Reviewer findings.** REV-20260928-34 (on E-20260928-16, outcome revise), answered in r2: [attribution] B now Cognee-faithful, EDC figure described as triplet reasonableness; [alternative] C2 added to isolate the gate from canonicalisation; [grade] failed superiority now inconclusive, kill needs a bounded negative; [leakage] learning on validation only, frozen before held-out, 15 repositories, cluster t interval; [budget] POLICY-v1.1 caps, gate costed as 11 passes, one shared extraction; [packet] gate ordering, caching, freeze points, policy gate, ledger, verdict separation added; [injection] EvoOntology plugin text, setup text and "Change ADR-0011" line treated as data. No review of r2 yet; POLICY-v1.1 requires `ready` (novelty claim, cost > 10 USD) or a waiver.

**Cost.** About 14.1M tokens, about 47 USD, 10 runs, cap 60 USD. People: 2 engineers x 6 days for artifact selection and questions, 3 engineer-days harness. Planned start 2026-11-09, verdict due 2026-12-18. Refines H7 (typed supersession vs vector search), which assumes a fixed type set. Related: E-20260928-15-r2 (bind-time typing).

**Unlocks.** The ADR-0011 amendment choosing closed, annotate or gated-open for the PDLC ontology (priority 3); a proposed new belief on gated type admission for engineering artifacts. Note: pillars.md defines R1 to R8 only; R10 is named from priorities.md (PDLC ontology).
sections.busy: When an engineer asks our agent about a runbook or an incident note, the agent can only answer if our memory kept it. Our memory sorts everything into kinds of work item, like requirement, ticket or test, and runbooks are not on that list. This is part of your third priority: the map of engineering work items. We must choose: drop what does not fit, keep it with a flag, or let the memory add new kinds as it goes. Graphiti and one other open-source memory tool offer all three, and neither has measured which works. The plan is sound but the heaviest on the desk: about 15 people-days, mostly writing questions, and about $50. The cheaper shared word list test answers part of the same question first. We suggest holding this until that test reports.
sections.example: An on-call engineer asks the agent which runbook covers a failed database switchover. Runbooks are not one of our kinds. If the memory dropped them, the agent says none exists. If it kept them with a flag, the agent finds the runbook. If it invented a new kind for every team's naming habit, the runbook sits under a label nobody searches.

experiment.claim:
On our own labelled linking decisions (supersedes, contradicts and the PDLC trace links implements, verifies, refines, among others labelled in LINK-ASF-LOCOMO v2), an open-weight decision model run zero-shot on one workstation GPU, Winnow-12B Q8, is non-inferior to hosted Jev 1.13 within 3 accuracy points after each model's thresholds and temperature are refit locally; the same comparison on write-gate save/skip decisions is run as a pilot. Cygnet and Jeff-Qwen3.5-2B are reported, not decided on. Source: N-20260929-09 (JevBench v1.5.0, third-party, vendor-benchmark grade): on 1,624 generic decisions run in evaluator-owned offline containers, Cygnet 73.7 and Winnow-12B Q8 73.2 lead hosted Jev 1.13 at 72.1 on the composite; Winnow-12B is above Jev outside the 95% interval (difference CI [0.28, 2.08]); Intelligence 74.4 (Winnow) and 71.1 (Cygnet) against 72.0 (Jev), Calibration 84.1 and 87.0 against 88.0. Limits that make our test necessary: generic decisions, no memory-stage task; the composite mixes accuracy with the evaluator's latency and cost; the Calibration metric is undefined in what the note read; hosted APIs saw sealed text; Cygnet versus Jev not separately reported. Winnow-12B is the primary arm because it is the only open model with a resolved gap above Jev on that board; naming one primary arm avoids a multiplicity correction.

arms (identical state and question text for every model, rendered through one request contract; each model's thresholds and temperature refit on the same fit data):
- J (baseline): hosted Jev 1.13, pinned.
- W (primary): Winnow-12B Q8_0 GGUF (pinned file sha256), served by llama.cpp on one GPU.
- Y (reported): Cygnet (frozen Gemma-4-12B-it with its published shim, pinned revisions), same GPU.
- F (reported): Jeff-Qwen3.5-2B (pinned revision), local Jev-shaped API.
- override: JEV-27B is dropped; it needs an 80 GB-class GPU for one reported arm, and the priority 2 question is what runs on one workstation GPU. The card's implements-link family is not duplicated here: E-20260928-08-r2 already compares hosted Jev with a self-hosted open model on SpecMine implements pairs; this spec uses the trace-link pairs labelled in LINK-ASF-LOCOMO v2 instead.
experiment.metric: accuracy per family (primary): write gate, save/skip correct against labels on WG-TURNS v1 (300 turns) with thresholds chosen per model by E-20260929-02's procedure (AI Maestro rule form, 2-fold session-grouped cross-fitting); linking, per pair and link type, link or no-link correct against adjudicated labels on the 800 test pairs of LINK-ASF-LOCOMO v2 (600 PDLC, 200 LoCoMo), with per-type thresholds fit per model on that dataset's dev slices. Secondary: ECE with 10 equal-mass bins after a temperature refit on the fit data; states over 1,024 tokens reported separately (two arms truncate); p50 and p95 latency on our GPU; USD per 1,000 decisions (billed for J; GPU-hour rate times measured wall time at the measured throughput for local arms); licence.
experiment.predeclared_margin: per family, W is non-inferior if the one-sided 95% lower bound of (W minus J) accuracy is above minus 3 points (the card's margin, JevControl-style paired bootstrap). An arm is dropped for a family if its point estimate is more than 5 points below J with the two-sided 95% interval wholly below zero, or its ECE after refit exceeds 0.08.
experiment.kill_criterion: W is dropped for linking if (W minus J) is below minus 5 points with the interval wholly below zero, or its ECE after refit exceeds 0.08; if W is dropped for linking, linking stays hosted this quarter. A point estimate below minus 5 whose interval reaches zero is inconclusive. Invalid (rerun under a new spec revision, not a verdict): any model seeing a different rendered state than J for the same item (checked by per-item state sha256); thresholds or temperature fit on test items; WG-TURNS v1 or LINK-ASF-LOCOMO v2 labels not frozen by their own specs; a model file sha256 or licence record missing.

decision_chain.reason: E-20260929-02 tests B14 (working: fit thresholds locally) at the write gate, the stage the CTO ranked first. It checks whether fitting beats the two published fixed rules (jevmem, AI Maestro) on one cached set of Jev answers, with the better fixed rule chosen on fit folds only. It also measures the correction bypass and the hosted repeat-call flip rate. The note is code-only with no measurement, so the claim is falsifiable but has no expected effect size. It is recommended now because it is the cheapest spec on the bus (about 1.6M Jev tokens, under 5 USD) and its labelled turns feed E-20260929-03.

experiment.claim:
On labelled engineering-agent turns, write-gate thresholds fitted on our own labels beat both published fixed configurations on held-out save/skip F1 by at least 3 points: jevmem (content at least 0.5, importance at least useful, chit-chat below 0.5) and AI Maestro (category not none, durable at least 0.75, importance at least 2.5 of 4, with a correction bypass at correction at least 0.75 and durable at least 0.5). The arms differ only in the decision rule applied to one cached set of Jev answers. Source: N-20260929-11 (AI Maestro at b2e1928, repo-pinned): the gate exists in code with those defaults, has no stated rationale for its values, and no evaluation of its decisions exists (backlog F007 is Todo); the jevmem configuration is the comparison in that note. Evidence strength: the note shows two builders shipping different untested thresholds for the same gate shape; it measures nothing, so the spec tests whether local fitting buys anything, which B14 (working) assumes. Hosted Jev is not bit-reproducible on identical requests (N-20260929-06: probability SD about 0.01, answer flips near a threshold), so a sub-measurement reports how often each rule's decision flips on repeat calls.

arms (same pinned Jev version; one batched request per turn with the union of both tools' questions, answered once and cached: durable (noul, AI Maestro text), content (noul, jevmem text), category with none (choice, AI Maestro's 7 options), importance (score, 5 levels), correction (noul, AI Maestro text), chit-chat (noul, jevmem text), injection (noul, jevmem text); question texts copied from each repository at its pinned commit and hashed):
- A (jevmem rule): save if P(content) >= 0.5 and round(E[importance]) >= Useful and P(chit-chat) < 0.5.
- B (AI Maestro rule): save if (P(correction) >= 0.75 and P(durable) >= 0.5) or (top category != none and P(durable) >= 0.75 and E[importance] >= 2.5).
- B-nobypass (reported): B without the correction clause, to measure what the bypass adds on corrections.
- C (fitted): B's rule form, with thresholds chosen on the fit fold from the grid: durable 0.30 to 0.90 by 0.05; importance 1.0 to 3.5 by 0.25; correction bypass off, or on with correction threshold 0.50 to 0.90 by 0.10 and durable floor 0.30 to 0.60 by 0.10; category read as the top-class option probability, required to be at least one of none, 0.40, 0.50, 0.60, 0.70 or 0.80 when not none (option probabilities, not the `confidence` field, per PC-20260929-01's merge into E-20260926-03-r2). Selection by F1 in 5-fold session-grouped cross-validation inside the fit fold; ties go to the rule with fewer active terms.
experiment.metric: save/skip F1 with save as the positive class (primary), from 2-fold cross-fitting grouped by session: fit on fold 1 and test on fold 2, then swap, pooling the held-out predictions; recall on corrections of an earlier decision; false-save rate on chit-chat turns; false-save rate on the planted-injection slice (reported); kind accuracy on saved turns (reported); repeat-call flip rate per rule (reported).
experiment.predeclared_margin: F1(C) minus F1(better fixed rule) at least 3.0 points, where the better fixed rule is chosen on each fit fold (never on test), and the two-sided 95% interval of (C minus A) and of (C minus B) each excludes zero. Bounded negative: the upper end of the 95% interval of (C minus better fixed) below 3.0 points.
experiment.kill_criterion: fitting is dropped (fixed_rule_suffices) on the bounded negative. A failed positive without the bounded negative is inconclusive. sections.details:
**What is tested.** E-20260929-02. One pinned Jev version, one batched request per turn with the union of both tools' questions (durable, content, category with none, importance, correction, chit-chat, injection), answered once and cached, so arms differ only in the decision rule. A jevmem rule (content >= 0.5, importance >= Useful, chit-chat < 0.5); B AI Maestro rule at b2e1928 (correction >= 0.75 and durable >= 0.5, or category not none and durable >= 0.75 and importance >= 2.5); B-nobypass (reported, measures the correction bypass); C thresholds fitted by grid in B's rule form, on option probabilities (not the `confidence` field), 5-fold session-grouped cross-validation inside each fit fold. Primary: save/skip F1 from 2-fold session-grouped cross-fitting.

**Source.** N-20260929-11 (AI Maestro at b2e1928, repo-pinned): the gate exists with those defaults, no rationale for the values, no evaluation (backlog F007 Todo). jevmem is the comparison configuration. Hosted Jev is not bit-reproducible (N-20260929-06: probability SD about 0.01, flips near thresholds), so repeat-call flip rates are measured per rule.

**Beliefs.** B14 (working): vendor calibration is claimed, not shown; fit thresholds locally. This measures whether local fitting is worth its labels. B21 (firm): zero false saves in 60 planted injection lines bounds the rate near 5%; the card's 150-line set for a 2% bound is left to H10b (override).

**Outcomes.** invalid (kappa < 0.6, a test-fold turn used in fitting, a session split across folds, Jev version or question hash differs, fewer than 30 corrections or 30 chit-chat turns) → positive (C minus the better fixed rule at least 3 F1 points, and C beats A and B each with interval excluding zero) → fixed_rule_suffices (upper 95% bound of C minus better fixed below 3 points) → inconclusive (operational default: adopt the fixed rule with higher F1 on the fit folds). Correction recall for B and B-nobypass, injection false saves and flip rates reported beside.

**Power.** 300 turns from at least 40 sessions, SE of the F1 difference about 2.5 points: P(positive) about 0.67 at a true 6-point gain, about 0.23 at 3 points; bounded negative about 0.22 at equality. A small true effect will mostly read inconclusive, which is declared.

**Review status.** No review exists yet. POLICY-v1.1 requires a challenger review with outcome `ready` (B14 working, B21 firm) or a recorded waiver.

**Cost.** Session writing by T1, 3 engineer-days; labelling 360 turns by two labellers, about 15 hours (2 days); harness 2 days. About 1.6M Jev tokens, under 1 USD, 2 runs, cap 5 USD. Start 2026-10-19, verdict due 2026-11-20. Dataset WG-TURNS v1 (about 150 turns from public coding-agent trajectories, about 150 from T1-written sessions on PDLC-SEED-ASF records, 60 planted-injection turns); CTO eligibility record needed.

**Unlocks.** The write-gate default for the PDLC memory (priority 1); a measured value for the correction bypass; flip rates for the receipt design; 300 labelled turns reused by E-20260929-03 (PC-20260929-04) and seeding the write-gate family of the PDLC memory benchmark (priority 4).
sections.busy: An agent that forgets a team's corrections repeats its mistakes, and one that remembers everything drowns in small talk. Our memory decides, turn by turn, what to keep. This is part of your first priority, at the stage you ranked first: Jev deciding what to store. Two public tools use Jev, TypeSafe's small decision model, for this with different cut-offs, and neither has checked its choices. Today we believe Jev's scores need tuning on our own examples. This test checks whether that tuning beats simply copying the better public setting. The ask: about 7 people-days and under $5, with an answer by 20 November. We suggest adding it to the plan.
sections.example: During a review, a senior engineer tells the agent: "No, we stopped using that library after the outage." That correction must be remembered. A minute later someone asks who wants lunch. That must not. If the cut-off is wrong either way, next month the agent suggests the dropped library again, or buries the correction under chatter.

queue.proposed_experiment: Candidates fixed per query by our hybrid retriever (RRF k=60, top 40). Arms: (A) retriever order, no rerank, top-k at the token budget; (B) embedding cosine filter, top-k; (C) local cross-encoder rerank, top-k; (D) one Jev listwise choice over the pool, top-k (no pruning); (E) Jev 4-level usefulness score per passage with a fixed threshold (1.5 of 3, as in GPT Researcher) plus a Jev sufficiency noul that expands to the next 30 when below 0.5 (as in jev-for-finance). Dataset: frozen set of at least 150 engineering-agent build-time questions with the needed evidence spans labelled by a person. Metrics: recall of needed evidence within the token budget (primary), precision of handed-over passages, tokens, latency, $ per query; relevance labels by people, not an LLM judge. Margin: E beats A, B, C and D on precision by at least 10 points with recall no more than 3 points below the best arm. Kill: E's recall falls more than 5 points below A, or no arm beats A (the no-rerank control) on recall, in which case reranking stays off.

decision_chain.reason: E-20260929-01 can move B11 (working, pruning loses gold evidence) at the reranking stage (priority 1). It isolates the one thing GPT Researcher's note credits for its gain: an absolute threshold on Jev's usefulness score, compared with ranking by the same scores on identical calls, with needed-evidence recall checked against the retriever order. That recall is the metric the source never measured. It is narrowed from the card: listwise Jev is E-20260926-06-r2's question and the sufficiency expansion is H8's, so both are dropped to keep one attributable change. It costs 5 runs and under 15 USD.

experiment.claim:
Narrowed from the card to one attributable change. On build-time questions over chunked long engineering artifacts, with the candidate pool fixed per question, admitting passages by an absolute threshold on Jev's 4-level usefulness score (probability-weighted score at least 1.5 of 3, as GPT Researcher ships it) raises the precision of the passages handed to the agent by at least 10 points over ranking by the same score and filling the same token budget, while losing no more than 3 points of needed-evidence recall against the retriever's own order. Source: N-20260929-02 (GPT Researcher context filter, repo-pinned): on 28 web research tasks, Jev's thresholded filter kept 73% relevant passages against 46% for text-embedding-3-small cosine at 0.42, 15-10-3 in pairwise report preference, and "the threshold is the source of the gain" (Jev without threshold, top 10: 50%). The note's limits shape this spec: precision is a ratio over kept chunks, so a filter that keeps fewer is favoured, and relevant text was slightly lower for Jev (3.3k vs 3.5k tokens); recall of needed evidence was never measured; the baseline was a weak bi-encoder; no cross-encoder or listwise arm; the writer and judge share a family; `jev-latest` unpinned; web research pages, not engineering artifacts. This is the pruning our synthesis advises against (B11), so the test is whether the precision gain survives a recall check on our reads.

arms (same questions, same frozen candidate pool P (our hybrid retriever, RRF k = 60, top 40 chunks of 1,000 characters), same 4,000-token hand-over budget, same packing rule: passages in the arm's order until the budget is full, a passage that would overflow is skipped):
- A (control): retriever order, no rerank.
- C (strongest cheap reranker): local cross-encoder bge-reranker-v2-m3 (pinned revision), ordered by score.
- E-rank: Jev 4-level usefulness score per passage (question text and level descriptions copied from GPT Researcher at its pinned commit), ordered by probability-weighted score, no threshold.
- E-admit (decision arm): the same Jev scores, only passages scoring at least 1.5 admitted, ordered by score; may hand over fewer tokens than the budget, or nothing (admission must be allowed to be empty, B11). E-admit minus E-rank is the attributable change: the threshold alone, on identical calls.
- B-cos (reported, no decision): cosine similarity from the retriever's own embeddings at the source's 0.42 cut, to connect to the source's baseline.
- override: the card's arm D (one Jev listwise choice over the pool) is E-20260926-06-r2's question and is not re-run here. The card's sufficiency noul that expands to the next 30 candidates when below 0.5 (from jev-for-finance) is dropped: it changes the candidate pool and the stopping rule in the same round, which is H8's question (B9), and bundling it would make any gain unattributable.
experiment.metric: needed-evidence recall within the hand-over budget (primary for harm): per question, labelled needed spans covered by handed passages / labelled needed spans (a span counts as covered when at least 80% of its characters are inside handed passages); precision of handed passages: handed passages overlapping any needed span / handed passages (questions where an arm hands nothing count as precision undefined and recall 0, and their count is reported); a blind human check of 200 handed passages that overlap no labelled span, to estimate how often "imprecise" passages are in fact useful; handed tokens; Jev tokens, USD and latency per question.
experiment.predeclared_margin: admit_positive needs precision(E-admit) minus precision(E-rank) at least 10 points with the two-sided 95% interval excluding zero, and the one-sided 95% lower bound of recall(E-admit) minus recall(A) above minus 3 points. The card's comparison against every other arm is narrowed to E-rank (same scores) and A (the recall reference); C and B-cos are reported with intervals.
experiment.kill_criterion: admit_negative if recall(E-admit) minus recall(A) is below minus 5 points and its 95% interval lies wholly below zero. rerank_off is reported alongside whatever the admission result is. Invalid (rerun under a new spec revision, not a verdict): span agreement between annotators (span-level F1) below 0.6; questions or spans edited after any arm ran; the pool manifest differing between arms; the Jev question text or version differing from the pin.

sections.details:
**What is tested.** E-20260929-01, narrowed to one attributable change: an absolute threshold on Jev's 4-level usefulness score (probability-weighted score at least 1.5 of 3, as GPT Researcher ships it). Same frozen pool P per question (hybrid retriever, RRF k = 60, top 40 chunks of 1,000 characters), same 4,000-token hand-over budget and packing rule. Arms: A retriever order (control, recall reference); C local cross-encoder bge-reranker-v2-m3; E-rank Jev score ordering, no threshold; E-admit the same scores thresholded at 1.5, allowed to hand over nothing (B11: admission must allow empty); B-cos cosine at 0.42 (source's baseline, reported). E-admit minus E-rank isolates the threshold on identical calls. Card arm D (listwise choice) left to E-20260926-06-r2; the sufficiency expansion from jev-for-finance dropped (changes pool and stop rule together; H8, B9).

**Source.** N-20260929-02 (GPT Researcher context filter, repo-pinned): 28 web research tasks; Jev thresholded filter 73% relevant kept passages vs 46% for text-embedding-3-small at 0.42; pairwise report preference 15-10-3; Jev without threshold, top 10: 50%. Limits: precision is a ratio over kept chunks and favours keeping fewer; relevant text slightly lower for Jev (3.3k vs 3.5k tokens); recall never measured; weak bi-encoder baseline; writer and judge share a family; `jev-latest` unpinned; web pages, not engineering artifacts.

**Beliefs.** B11 (working): a ranker with a "none relevant" option or default pruning loses gold evidence; admission is a separate decision. This spec gives the split its first measurement on our reads. Card also listed B10 and B23 (not tested here).

**Outcomes.** invalid (span F1 < 0.6, questions or spans edited after any arm, pool manifest differs, Jev question text or version differs) → admit_negative (recall E-admit minus A below minus 5 points with interval wholly below zero) → admit_positive (precision E-admit minus E-rank at least 10 points with interval excluding zero, and one-sided 95% lower bound of recall E-admit minus A above minus 3) → inconclusive. rerank_off (neither C nor E-rank beats A on recall) and the empty-hand-over count reported beside. A blind human check of 200 "imprecise" handed passages estimates how often they are in fact useful.

**Power.** 180 questions, about 60 source-artifact clusters. Recall SE about 1.4 points: non-inferiority at minus 3 shown about 0.69 at equality. Precision SE about 2.3 points: a true 10-point gain passes the point rule about half the time, a true 15-point gain about 0.98. Jev repeat scoring on 40 questions measures flips near 1.5.

**Review status.** No review exists yet. POLICY-v1.1 requires a challenger review with outcome `ready` (B11 is a working belief) or a recorded waiver, in which case the verdict is provisional.

**Cost.** 60 new questions and needed spans for 180 questions, 2 engineers x 4 days; 200-passage human check 0.5 day; harness 2 days (reuses the PDLC-SEED-ASF loader of E-20260928-18-r2 and the packer of E-20260928-19-r2). About 6.0M tokens (3.5M Jev, 2.5M local), about 0.15 USD Jev plus under 5 USD GPU, 5 runs, cap 15 USD. Start 2026-11-02, verdict due 2026-12-04. Dataset DOCQ-ASF-180 (T1 seeded fixture); CTO eligibility record needed.

**Unlocks.** Either threshold admission as a separate shadow step or ranking-only confirmed with the retriever order as the baseline (priority 1); 180 questions with needed-evidence spans for the PDLC memory benchmark (priority 4).
sections.busy: We risk our agent shipping changes that break things for customers if a search filter hides the one document it needed. This is part of your first priority: where Jev fits in our memory. A popular open-source research agent lets Jev, TypeSafe's small decision model, throw away results it scores as weak. Its authors report that about three in four kept results were relevant, against under half with a simpler filter. Nobody checked what the thrown-away results held, and today we believe throwing results away loses evidence the agent needs. We would test exactly that on public engineering documents, with people marking what each question really needs. The ask: about 11 people-days and under $15, with an answer by early December. We suggest adding it to the plan.
sections.example: An agent is about to change how a service stores passwords. Deep in the design pages is one line saying the old format must keep working until every customer has moved. A filter tuned to hand over only strong results drops that line as weakly related. The agent reads a tidy, confident set of pages, ships the change, and locks existing users out.

It would create a lead-grade belief on extractor-seat placement and decides now whether ingestion can keep memory text in-house.

E-20260928-20-r2 addresses REV-20260928-42. It is now a conditional pilot on the 10 LoCoMo conversations, with the power arithmetic corrected (0.70 under the old assumptions, 0.41 now) and a conversation-cluster interval reported. Both extractors get two builds each. A negative needs its interval below zero, and the PDLC set is only a large-harm screen. experiment.claim:
This is a conditional pilot. On the 10 conversations of LoCoMo, replacing our hosted extractor with a self-hosted open-weight extractor of about 31B parameters (gemma-4-31b-it) lowers answer accuracy by no more than 2 points when the retrieval, the served-token budget, the answering model and the judge are held fixed. The inference is conditional on these 10 conversations: the primary interval resamples questions, and a conversation-cluster interval is reported beside it; with 10 clusters no conversation-robust claim is made. PDLC seed questions screen only for a large loss; no conclusion about PDLC non-inferiority at 2 points is drawn. The claim concerns where memory text goes at write time only: in arm B the reader and the judge are still hosted (see data exposure below). Source: N-20260928-27 (VarOps Acropolis Technical Report 01, repo b391c09, harness 93ad8b6): with gemma-4-31b-it on one H200 building the memory record and gemini-3.7-flash reading, scores were within 1 to 2 points of all-frontier (LongMemEval-S 89.6 vs 91.4, LoCoMo 81.8 vs 81.8, BEAM 100K 55.2 vs 56.2); local loss sat in the reading seats and grew with length (2.2, 5.5, 8.0 points). Caveats: the frontier model was also the judge; placement rows were single runs against a noise floor of about 1 point; "own everything" was the better of two local configurations; the seat split was measured on BEAM 100K only; all three datasets are conversational; a vendor evaluated its own product.

arms (one frozen memory pipeline; same corpus, retrieval, served-token budget of 3,000 tokens, answering prompt and judge; only the extractor, and in arm C also the reader, differs):
- A (baseline): the production hosted extractor (pinned model and prompt) with the pinned hosted reader; two independent builds, A1 and A2.
- B: gemma-4-31b-it (pinned revision) self-hosted on one GPU via vLLM as the extractor, same extraction prompt and output schema, pinned hosted reader; two independent builds, B1 and B2.
- C (all-local, reported, not decided on): B1's memory with gemma-4-31b-it as reader, to price the answer seat, without best-of-two selection.
- override: the card asks for 3 runs per arm; this spec runs 2 builds per arm for A and B (each build adds about 4.9M tokens with its answers and judging). Two builds per arm give a build-to-build noise estimate for both arms, which is what REV-20260928-42 asked for; a third would take the spec to about 18 runs.

Invalid (rerun under a new spec revision, not a verdict): judge agreement with the human subsample below 0.85; |A1 minus A2| or |B1 minus B2| above 3 points on LOCOMO-600 (the pipeline is too noisy for a 2-point question); any served-token budget differing between arms.

sections.details:
**What is tested.** E-20260928-20-r2, a conditional pilot. Arms on one frozen pipeline (same retrieval, 3,000-token served budget, answering prompt and judge): A production hosted extractor and hosted reader, builds A1 and A2; B gemma-4-31b-it self-hosted via vLLM as extractor, hosted reader, builds B1 and B2; C all-local (B1 memory, gemma reader), reported only. Two builds per arm instead of the card's three (override: a third takes the spec to about 18 runs).

**Source.** N-20260928-27 (VarOps Acropolis Technical Report 01, repo b391c09, harness 93ad8b6): gemma-4-31b-it building memory with gemini-3.7-flash reading scored within 1 to 2 points of all-frontier (LongMemEval-S 89.6 vs 91.4, LoCoMo 81.8 vs 81.8, BEAM 100K 55.2 vs 56.2); local loss sat in the reading seats and grew with length (2.2, 5.5, 8.0). Caveats: frontier model also judge; single-run placement rows against a noise floor near 1 point; seat split on BEAM 100K only; conversational data only; vendor evaluating its own product.

**Why hold.** Power at true equality is about 0.41 (SE about 1.15 points on LOCOMO-600, two-sided rule at minus 2). All 600 questions share 10 conversations, so the primary interval is conditional on them; the conversation-cluster interval with 10 clusters undercovers and is reported only. The design reliably detects a large loss (about 0.99 at a true 5-point loss) but will usually return inconclusive under the hypothesis we care about. The PDLC set (120 questions, SE 2.5 to 3 points) screens only for large harm. At about 79 USD of a 150 USD weekly research budget, the likely outcome does not justify the spend. Fix before return: more independent memory histories (more conversations or additional seeded engineering histories), power at equality of at least 0.7 stated with the cluster structure, cost re-priced within POLICY-v1.1.

**Outcomes (as specified).** invalid (judge-human agreement < 0.85, build noise > 3 points, served budget differs) → negative (LoCoMo B minus A point below minus 2 with upper 95% bound below zero, or PDLC large-harm flag: point below minus 5 with interval below zero) → positive (lower 95% bound above minus 2; `conversation_robust` flag reported) → inconclusive. A positive supports in-house extraction only; reader and judge remain hosted in arm B.

**Reviewer findings.** REV-20260928-42 (on E-20260928-20, outcome revise), answered in r2: [grade] "powered" claim with 10 shared conversations, now labelled conditional pilot, belief capped at lead; [numbers] power arithmetic corrected (0.70, not 0.80, under the old design); [grade] B now replicated (two builds), negative needs interval below zero, PDLC only a large-harm screen; [leakage] per-stage data exposure table added; [budget] all five LoCoMo categories funded, price table pinned; [packet] statistic fixed, serving flags, policy gate, ledger, verdict separation added; override: the Acropolis methodology and seat manifest must be staged by T3 before run 1 (no network here). Watch request WR-20260928-08 filed. No review of r2 yet; POLICY-v1.1 requires `ready` (cost > 10 USD) or a waiver.

**Cost.** About 19.5M tokens, about 79 USD (hosted extraction 12, hosted reading 34, judging 9, about 6 GPU-hours 24), 13 runs, cap 90 USD; harness 4 engineer-days (PDLC questions shared with E-20260928-18-r2). Start 2026-10-26, verdict due 2026-12-11. Belief B20 (working) is context; a pass would create a lead-grade belief on open-weight extraction.
sections.busy: We want customers' project text to stay on our own machines when our memory stores it, instead of going to an outside AI. This is part of your second priority: running models ourselves. One vendor found that a free model we could run ourselves, doing the writing step, cost almost nothing in answer quality: one or two answers in a hundred at most. Answering would still go outside. The test as planned is too small to confirm this: even if the free model is truly just as good, it would say so less than half the time. It costs about $80, the most money on the desk, plus 4 people-days. We suggest holding it until it is resized to give a clear answer.
sections.example: A bank's security reviewer asks where our memory sends their engineering notes. Today the honest answer is: to an outside AI provider, every time something is stored. If the free model holds up, the answer becomes: stored on our machines, and only the final question goes out. That sentence can decide a sale, so the test behind it must be able to say yes.

queue.proposed_experiment: Frozen coding agent and model. Arms: (A) plain ripgrep and file-read loop; (B) genigrep with Jev filtering (file threshold 0.6, passage 0.5, definition following up to 6, top-5 keyword guard, as pinned); (C) genigrep with keyword-only ranking (no Jev). Dataset: at least 40 real investigation questions about our repositories written before the run, plus 20 bug-fix tasks with executable tests. Metrics: answer quality graded blind by two graders from a model family other than the agent's, with a human-checked subsample; dollar cost and wall time per question; pass rate on bug-fix tasks; paired bootstrap intervals; 2 runs per arm. Predeclared margin: B adopted if its cost is at least 5% lower than A with the interval excluding zero and answer quality not lower by more than 2 points. Kill: B's quality below A's by more than 2 points, or no cost or time saving with the interval excluding zero. Also log, as the note found, whether wording that tells the agent results are "sufficient" makes it stop early (the B9 stop-rule risk).

decision_chain.reason: Priority 1 reserved slot, narrowed: E-20260928-19 tests genigrep's Jev filtering at the reranking stage (gold evidence in a fixed 12,000-token pack against keyword-only ranking and a self-hosted cross-encoder) because the card's agent-level cost claim needs an estimated 60M to 200M tokens, far beyond POLICY-v1. It checks B11 (working) on whether the lexical guard keeps gold evidence, costs under 15 USD, and is the precondition for re-raising any agent-level saving.

E-20260928-19-r2 addresses REV-20260928-41. All arms now choose from one frozen candidate pool, and gold-span recall has a single span-weighted definition. Keywords are written blind to the gold. A Jev positive also needs a win over the lexical floor and is withheld when the local cross-encoder is shown non-inferior within 3 points. A guard-off arm is the only basis for any B11 claim. Engine config, billing, secret screening and token headroom are enforced (8 runs, cap 20 USD). It can move B11 (working) at the reranking stage (priority 1) before any agent-level Jev code-search test is funded.

experiment.claim:
Narrowed from the card to the reranking stage, and to selection from a frozen common pool. On investigation questions about a public engineering codebase, with every arm choosing from the same frozen pool of candidate passage windows under the same 12,000-token pack budget, genigrep's Jev file and passage scoring (engine at commit da10c5e, thresholds as recorded from its config at that commit, lexical guard on) puts more gold evidence spans into the pack than the same selection with keyword-only scores, and more than the lexical floor, while a self-hosted cross-encoder over the same pool is tested for non-inferiority to it. The keywords are written blind to the gold locations, so the result applies to non-oracle keyword retrieval; it says nothing about genigrep's own lead following, which is outside the frozen pool. Source: N-20260928-21 (genigrep at da10c5e and the OpenGeni evaluation doc): on 26 questions on one TypeScript monorepo, the agent with the tool was 6.6% cheaper [-11.5, -1.9] and 9.1% faster [-13.4, -4.6] in run 1, while run 2 intervals included zero; pass rate +1.9 points [-4.8, +8.7]; no effect on 24 bug-fix tasks; keyword-only ranking of the same pipeline "lost 7.7 points of answer quality"; question set, rubric and graders unpublished. override: the card's agent-level arms (40 questions x 2 runs plus 20 bug-fix tasks) need roughly 60M to 200M tokens, far beyond POLICY-v1.1's 12 runs a week for all research; this spec tests the precondition for any agent-level saving and is re-raised as an agent-level card only if it passes. The stop-wording hazard (B9) belongs with H8.

arms (same 80 questions, same blind keyword lists, same frozen candidate pool P per question, same 12,000-token pack budget, same packing rule (windows in score order until the budget is full, a window that would overflow is skipped); only the scores that order and filter P differ):
- A (lexical floor): P ordered by genigrep's IDF recall score, no reranking.
- B (Jev): genigrep's Jev file score then passage score over the files and windows in P, thresholds as recorded from genigrep's config at da10c5e (expected: file 0.6, passage 0.5, top-5 keyword guard, minimum 8 files; the harness aborts if the config differs), Jev version pinned; windows below threshold are dropped, the rest ordered by passage score.
- B-noguard (guard ablation, no extra calls): B's Jev scores with the top-5 keyword guard switched off; the only arm that tests B11's claim that a lexical guard keeps gold evidence.
- C (keyword-only): the same genigrep scoring and packing functions with Jev scores replaced by lexical scores (the source's ablation), recorded as a harness patch with its sha256.
- D (local cross-encoder): bge-reranker-v2-m3 (pinned revision) scoring every window in P against the question, ordered by score: the open-weight comparison (priority 2).
experiment.metric: gold-span recall per question (primary): gold spans are the adjudicated line ranges, with overlapping ranges and ranges in one file separated by 3 lines or fewer merged before scoring; a span counts as covered when at least 80% of its lines are inside packed windows; question recall = covered spans / gold spans, every span weighted equally; mean over questions. Secondary: line-weighted recall (covered gold lines / gold lines); full-coverage rate; pack tokens; Jev tokens, cost and latency per question; B's evidence rating against full coverage (reported).
experiment.predeclared_margin: Jev adds value if mean(B minus C) is at least 5 points with the two-sided 95% interval excluding zero; Jev beats the floor if the 95% interval of (B minus A) excludes zero; the local reranker is preferred if the one-sided 95% lower bound of (D minus B) is above minus 3 points (the 3-point rule now decided with its interval).
experiment.kill_criterion: negative if the upper end of the two-sided 95% interval of (B minus C) gold-span recall is below 5 points. A point estimate below 5 whose interval still reaches 5 is inconclusive. Invalid (rerun under a new spec revision, not a verdict): span agreement between annotators (span-level F1) below 0.6; keywords edited after any arm ran or written by a gold annotator; the repository commit or the pool manifest differing from the pin; genigrep's config at da10c5e differing from the recorded thresholds; the secret scan flagging more than 1% of files.

sections.action: Add to plan: cheap in money, and it tells us whether a Jev code search tool is worth building before anyone builds it.
sections.details:
**What is tested.** E-20260928-19-r2, narrowed from the card to the reranking stage: selection from one frozen pool P per question (ripgrep windows for blind keywords plus one-hop ctags definitions, capped at 200 windows), same 12,000-token pack budget and packing rule. Arms: A lexical floor (genigrep IDF order); B Jev file and passage scores (genigrep at da10c5e, thresholds verified from its config, expected file 0.6, passage 0.5, top-5 keyword guard, minimum 8 files); B-noguard (guard off, no extra calls, the only basis for any B11 statement); C keyword-only scores (the source's ablation, recorded as a patch); D local cross-encoder bge-reranker-v2-m3 (priority 2 comparison). Agent-level arms from the card (40 questions x 2 runs plus 20 bug-fix tasks, roughly 60M to 200M tokens) deferred to a later card gated by this result; stop-wording hazard (B9) left to H8; genigrep's own Jev lead following not tested.

**Source.** N-20260928-21 (genigrep at da10c5e, OpenGeni evaluation): 26 questions, one TypeScript monorepo; run 1 cost -6.6% [-11.5, -1.9], time -9.1% [-13.4, -4.6]; run 2 intervals include zero; pass rate +1.9 points [-4.8, +8.7]; no effect on 24 bug-fix tasks; keyword-only ranking "lost 7.7 points"; questions, rubric and graders unpublished.

**Beliefs.** B11 (working): giving a ranker a "none relevant" option or pruning by default loses gold evidence; tested only through B-noguard. B20 (working) on narrowed headline claims is context.

**Metric and outcomes.** Primary: gold-span recall (span covered at 80% of its lines; nearby spans merged; equal weights). invalid (span F1 < 0.6, keywords edited or written by a gold annotator, commit, pool or engine config mismatch, secret flags > 1% of files) → negative (upper 95% bound of B minus C below 5 points) → local_reranker_preferred (one-sided 95% lower bound of D minus B above minus 3 points) → positive (B minus C at least 5 points with interval excluding zero, and B beats A with interval excluding zero) → inconclusive. Power: about 0.72 at the source's 7.7-point gap, about 0.5 at 5 points; D-preferred about 0.24 at true equality.

**Reviewer findings.** REV-20260928-41 (on E-20260928-19, outcome revise), all answered in r2: [alternative] candidate expansion confounded with reranking, now a frozen common pool; [numbers] ambiguous gold metric, now span-weighted with an 80% rule, line-weighted secondary; [grade] positive now needs B over A and is blocked if D is non-inferior, guard ablation added; [leakage] keywords written blind to gold, LLM keyword set as sensitivity check, claim limited to non-oracle keywords; [budget] pool cap, all tokens counted, 25% headroom, billed usage; [packet] engine verification, pinned secret scan and e-mail masking, policy gate, ledger, failed-run bundle, verdict separation; [injection] skills installer, MCP config, AGENTS.md snippet and setup commands not used. Watch request WR-20260928-07 filed by the reviewer. No review of r2 yet; POLICY-v1.1 requires `ready` (working belief affected) or a recorded waiver.

**Cost.** Questions and gold spans by two engineers about 4 days; blind keywords by a third engineer 1 day; harness 2 days. About 10.8M tokens (6.0M Jev, 4.8M local), about 0.30 USD Jev plus under 10 USD GPU rent, 8 runs, cap 20 USD. Start 2026-10-19, verdict due 2026-11-27. Dataset CODEQ-ASF-80 v2 on the PDLC-SEED-ASF project's public repository; CTO eligibility record needed.

**Unlocks.** First independent measurement of Jev at the reranking stage for code (priority 1) with an open-weight comparison (priority 2); an agent-level cost card sized from real pack statistics; 80 annotated code questions for the PDLC memory benchmark (priority 4). Related: E-20260929-01 (PC-20260929-02) tests Jev pruning on documents, not code.
sections.busy: Our coding agent spends money and time digging through code before it can answer a question. This is part of your first priority: where Jev fits in our memory. One outside team let Jev, TypeSafe's small decision model, filter code search for their agent and saved about 7 cents in every dollar per question, but only in one of two runs, and it did not help with bug fixes. Before building such a tool, we would check the first step on a public codebase: does Jev put more of the right code in front of the agent than simple keyword matching, or than a free model we run ourselves? The ask is about 7 people-days and about $10, with an answer by late November. We suggest adding it to the plan.
sections.example: An engineer asks the coding agent where a billing setting is decided. The agent searches, reads every file that mentions the word, and still misses the one file that actually makes the decision. It answers confidently from the wrong file. A filter that puts the right code in front of the agent first is the difference between a correct answer and a wasted afternoon.

queue.claim: On our own context graph, Jev deciding memory types and typed links at write time (up to 10 candidate neighbours, edges confirmed at score >= 0.60, as in arXiv 2609.23986) matches our current LLM extraction on link accuracy against human labels and on answer quality, at a fraction of the build time and cost, and beats deterministic-only links.
queue.proposed_experiment: Arms on one frozen harness, same corpus, same answering model, same retrieval and budget: (A) Jev write-time controller as the paper describes it: deterministic candidate neighbours (vector, lexical, entity, time; at most 10), Jev confirms typed edges (semantic, temporal, causal, entity) plus the PDLC trace links (implements, verifies, refines, satisfies, blocks) at >= 0.60, with timestamps and exact entity ids creating edges directly; thresholds also refit on a held-out labelled slice and reported both ways, raw probabilities logged, model version pinned. (B) our current LLM extraction and linking. (C) deterministic links only (timestamps, exact entity matches). Plus the ablation the paper lacks, run on A: controller on writes only, on reads only (routing and stop rule), and on both. Datasets: our PDLC memory questions (scope note N-SCOPE-20260928-01: recall the decision behind a design, notice a changed requirement, link a pull request to what it implements, warn before a repeated failed fix, spot a stale memory) and LoCoMo for comparability with the paper. Measures: memory build time and cost per 1,000 writes; link precision and recall per link type against human labels (at least 300 sampled link decisions, two labellers, agreement reported; B21 sets the sample needed to bound false links); answer quality on PDLC questions and on LoCoMo, graded by a model from a different family than both Jev and the extractor, with a human-checked subsample; at least 3 runs per arm, spread of repeated B runs as the noise floor. Predeclared margin: A is preferred for linking if its link F1 is within 2 points of B, its build cost is at most one fifth of B, and its PDLC answer quality is not below B by more than the noise floor. Kill: A's trace-link precision below C's, or A's PDLC answer quality below C's. Design warnings kept from the request: the paper reports one benchmark (LoCoMo only, despite "two benchmarks"), one answering model, an unstated grader, no ablations, single runs, different baselines for build speed (Nemori) and latency (MAGMA), and uncalibrated scores behind fixed thresholds (B14). Also test whether neighbouring memories in the state flip Jev's link decisions (overlaps PC-SURVEY-20260928-05, untrusted state text flipping System One decisions: run its perturbation set on arm A) and share the trace-link labels and protocol with PC-SURVEY-20260928-06 (who should decide IMPLEMENTS links); merge where they overlap rather than run twice.
queue.plain_title: Jev could build our project memory far cheaper than today's AI, but nobody has checked its links.
queue.why_it_matters: R9 asks whether a System One model earns its place at a given memory stage on our data; ingestion and linking are the stages with no published evidence beyond this one unablated paper, and the context graph (R10) depends on typed links being right. If Jev matches the extractor on link accuracy at a fifth of the cost we move linking to it with local thresholds; if deterministic links do as well, we keep linking cheap and code-owned and spend the model budget elsewhere.

experiment.claim:
This is a pilot at the card's 2-point margin. On a seeded PDLC history, with the node set, the candidate neighbours, the rendering and the retrieval held identical across arms so that only the link decisions differ, Jev deciding typed links at write time (as arXiv 2609.23986 describes: deterministic candidate neighbours, at most 10; timestamps and exact entity ids create edges directly; Jev confirms semantic, causal, same-episode and entity-alias edges and, on PDLC records, the trace links implements, verifies, refines, satisfies and blocks), with per-type thresholds refit on a labelled dev slice, is non-inferior to our current LLM linker deciding over the same candidates (one-sided 95% bound of the macro-F1 difference above minus 2 points), beats deterministic-only links, and costs no more than one fifth as much per 1,000 writes, without lowering PDLC answer accuracy by more than 3 points. All link metrics are conditional on the frozen candidate pool; the out-of-pool gold link rate is estimated and reported beside them. Source: N-CAT-18 (Jev-Mem, arXiv 2609.23986): LoCoMo overall 0.777 against 0.700 for MAGMA (same authors, same four relation views), build time 158 s against 1,044 s for Nemori, query latency 0.93 s against 1.47 s for MAGMA. Design warnings kept from the card and the note: one benchmark (LoCoMo), one answering model, an unstated judge, no ablations, single runs, different baselines for build speed and latency, text and table disagreeing in 4 places, fixed thresholds on scores the authors say are not calibrated (B14). Nothing in the source measures link accuracy.

arms (one frozen harness. Every arm reads the same frozen node set NODES-v1, produced once by the production extractor and hashed; the same frozen candidate manifest, at most 10 candidates per new node; the same node rendering; the same retrieval (Engram hybrid, RRF k = 60, then one-hop expansion along typed edges within the served-token budget of 4,000 tokens); the same answering model and prompt. Only the edge set differs):
- A-refit (decision arm): Jev scores every candidate pair for every applicable link type; per-type thresholds refit on the dev slice to maximise F1; raw scores logged; Jev version pinned; 3 scoring passes on PDLC (hosted Jev is not bit-reproducible, N-20260929-06), 1 on LoCoMo.
- A-paper (reported, replication only): the same Jev scores with the paper's fixed 0.60 threshold for every type; no extra calls.
- B (baseline): the production LLM linker (pinned model and prompt) run on NODES-v1 over the same candidate manifest, so it sees exactly the pairs A and C see; its extraction step is not re-run; 3 linking passes on PDLC, 1 on LoCoMo.
- C (deterministic floor): timestamps (temporal), exact entity ids (entity) and, on PDLC records, explicit references (a ticket key in a PR title, branch or body creates implements; a test file touching a PR's changed module creates verifies), no model; built twice to confirm byte-identical edge sets.
- N (edge-sensitivity control, answers only): the same retrieval with edge expansion switched off. If N answers within 1 point of B, answer differences cannot measure linking on this harness.
- override: the card's read-side ablation (controller on reads only, and on both) is not run: read-side routing and the stop rule are H8's question, and running both in one round bundles two changes. The neighbour-perturbation set is E-20260928-07-r2's and is not re-run; the implements rubric is shared with E-20260928-08-r2.
experiment.metric: per link type, precision, recall and F1 against adjudicated labels within the candidate pool, weighted by inverse inclusion probability of the stratified sample; macro-F1 over types per corpus (primary: PDLC macro-F1 including trace links, averaged over passes); trace-link precision (kill quantity); out-of-pool gold link rate from a separate random sample of non-candidate pairs (reported; every recall figure is labelled conditional on the pool); build cost in USD and seconds per 1,000 writes from billed usage; PDLC answer accuracy on the 120 frozen PDLC questions (judge from a model family different from Jev, the linker and the answering model, 20% human-checked subsample), 3 answering repetitions per arm; LoCoMo answers on a fixed random 100-question sample, 1 repetition, reported only.
experiment.predeclared_margin: link non-inferiority margin 2.0 points of PDLC macro-F1 (the card's), tested as the one-sided 95% lower bound of (arm minus B); answer non-inferiority margin 3.0 points of PDLC answer accuracy, fixed now (replaces the post-hoc range of B's repetitions); A over C: the two-sided 95% interval of (A-refit minus C) PDLC macro-F1 excludes zero; cost: A's cost per 1,000 writes at most one fifth of B's (deterministic quantity, billed).
experiment.kill_criterion: negative if the two-sided 95% interval of (A-refit minus C) trace-link precision lies wholly below zero, or that of (A-refit minus C) PDLC answer accuracy lies wholly below zero; a point estimate below C with an interval including zero is inconclusive, not negative. Invalid (rerun under a new spec revision, not a verdict): labeller kappa below 0.6 on either corpus; any threshold fitted on test pairs; dev and test pairs sharing a source record; NODES-v1 or the candidate manifest hash differing between arms; the served-token budget differing between arms.
