sections.action: Add to plan: it is the only test of Jev at the linking stage, and its hand-checked connections feed the open-model comparison and our own memory benchmark.
sections.details:
**What is tested.** E-20260928-18-r2 (pilot at the card's 2-point margin). Arms on one frozen node set (NODES-v1) and one frozen candidate manifest (at most 10 candidates per new node), same rendering, same retrieval (hybrid, RRF k = 60, one-hop typed-edge expansion inside a 4,000-token served budget), same answering model: A-refit (Jev confirms typed edges and the PDLC trace links implements, verifies, refines, satisfies, blocks; per-type thresholds refit on a dev slice split by source record and calendar month), A-paper (fixed 0.60, reported only), B (production LLM linker over the same candidates), C (deterministic: timestamps, exact entity ids, explicit ticket and test references), N (no-edge retrieval, detects a harness where edges do not affect answers). Read-side controller ablation dropped (H8's question); neighbour-perturbation set left to E-20260928-07-r2; implements rubric shared with E-20260928-08-r2.

**Source.** N-CAT-18, Jev-Mem (arXiv 2609.23986): LoCoMo 0.777 vs 0.700 for MAGMA, build 158 s vs 1,044 s for Nemori, latency 0.93 s vs 1.47 s for MAGMA. One benchmark, one answering model, unstated judge, no ablations, single runs, different baselines for speed and latency, text and tables disagree in 4 places, fixed thresholds on uncalibrated scores. No link-accuracy measurement exists anywhere.

**Beliefs.** B14 (working): vendor calibration is claimed, not shown; thresholds must be fitted locally. A pass adds a local threshold measurement. Would create a new belief on model-confirmed typed links at ingest.

**Outcomes (checked in this order).** invalid (kappa < 0.6, thresholds fit on test, dev/test share a record, node or candidate hashes or served budget differ) → negative (A-refit trace-link precision or PDLC answer accuracy below C with the two-sided 95% interval wholly below zero) → deterministic_suffices (C non-inferior to B within 2 points macro-F1 and 3 points answer accuracy) → positive (A-refit non-inferior to B within 2 points macro-F1 by one-sided 95% bound, beats C with interval excluding zero, cost at most one fifth of B per 1,000 writes, answers non-inferior within 3 points) → inconclusive. edges_inert reported beside the outcome.

**Power.** 600 labelled PDLC test pairs, SE about 1.8 points with design effect 1.3: P(pass) about 0.30 under equality, 0.72 at a true 2-point A advantage. A powered confirmatory run needs about 2,300 pairs per corpus. Expect inconclusive unless Jev is clearly better or clearly worse. About 150 trace pairs: zero false links bounds the rate near 2% (B21).

**Reviewer findings.** REV-20260928-40 (on E-20260928-18, outcome revise), all answered in r2: [alternative] only linking now differs (frozen nodes, candidates, rendering, retrieval; arm N added); [grade] deterministic sufficiency checked before positive and positive requires A over C; [grade] 2-point bound now enforced by the one-sided bound, answer margin fixed at 3 points in advance, negative needs intervals below zero; [baseline] recall labelled conditional on the candidate pool, 100 out-of-pool pairs estimate the missed-link rate, inverse-inclusion weights; [budget] 3 passes each for A and B, every phase priced, 14 runs, cap 80 USD; [packet] subcommands, seeds, grids, policy gate, ledger checks, failed-run bundles and verdict separation added, harness itself only after acceptance; [injection] README commands and Appendix B prompts treated as data. REV-20260928-37 was staged with this card but reviews E-20260928-13-r2 (Action-type preconditions); not applicable, though its dev/test split and explicit-inconclusive points were adopted. No review of r2 exists yet; POLICY-v1.1 requires a `ready` review (cost > 10 USD, working belief affected) or a recorded waiver, in which case the verdict is provisional.

**Cost.** Labelling 1,100 pairs by two labellers, about 60 labeller-hours (7.5 days); 120 PDLC questions, 2 engineer-days (shared with E-20260928-20-r2); harness 5 engineer-days. About 21.4M tokens, about 64 USD, 14 runs, cap 80 USD, at most 5 runs a week. Start 2026-10-26, verdict due 2026-12-18. Dataset LINK-ASF-LOCOMO v2 (PDLC-SEED-ASF built by T1 from one public ASF project, plus 2 LoCoMo conversations); CTO eligibility record needed before run 1.

**Unlocks.** First measurement of a System One model at the linking stage (priority 1) on PDLC trace links (priority 3); 900 labelled link pairs seeding the linking family of the PDLC memory benchmark (priority 4), reused by E-20260929-03 (PC-20260929-04).
sections.busy: Customers will trust our agent's answers about their projects only if its memory links the right things, such as which code change fixed which ticket. Today an expensive general AI draws those connections. This is part of your first priority: where Jev fits in our memory. Jev's own authors report that Jev, TypeSafe's small decision model, builds a memory about six times faster than a rival system, but nobody has checked whether its connections are right. We would compare Jev, today's AI and simple fixed rules on a public open-source project, with people marking which connections are correct. If the simple rules do as well, we keep them and spend nothing. The ask: about 15 people-days, mostly hand-checking, and about $65, with an answer by mid-December. We suggest adding it to the plan.
sections.example: A developer asks our agent why a login rule changed last spring. The memory should lead from the change to the ticket that asked for it and the test that checks it. If that connection is missing, the agent guesses. If a wrong connection was made, the agent cites the wrong ticket with confidence, and the developer fixes the wrong requirement.

queue.claim: Palantir and Fabric IQ both type data through a binding made once per source (column to property, identity key), not by tagging each item when it is served. Magneto shows a small retriever with a large-model rerank maps fields to types at 0.860 MRR, against about 0.35 for a classic matcher. LLM-only mapping falls from 0.79 at 23 target classes to 0.51 at 300. Our G7 is written as a Choice per item at serve time.
queue.proposed_experiment:
- **Setup.** Take three real backends (Jira, a GitHub repo, a Confluence space) and 300 served items, with a gold type and property for each item's key fields, labelled blind.
- **Arms.**
  - A: serve-time G7 Choice per item (Jev, fixed tag sets).
  - B: bind-time mapping. A small encoder retrieves the top 5 shared properties per source field, a typed Choice picks one, and a person confirms it once. Items are then typed by lookup.
  - C: B, plus serve-time A only for fields left unbound.
- Then change one source's schema (rename two Jira custom fields) and re-run.
- **Metrics.** Type accuracy on served items, serve-time p95 latency and cost per 1K items, and accuracy after the schema change with and without the binding migration rule.
- **Kill criterion.**
  - B or C is more than 3 points of type accuracy below A: keep G7 at serve time.
  - A is within 1 point of C and adds under 50 ms p95: bindings are not worth their upkeep; keep serve-time only.
  - The schema change silently mistypes more than 5% of items under B without a migration flag: the binding needs a breaking-change check before it ships.
queue.plain_title: Label each tool's fields once when connecting it, or every search result? The first is cheaper, if accurate.
queue.why_it_matters: This is the one gateway change the survey recommends (the ontology as a versioned per-backend contract). It needs a measurement before it goes into the design.

decision_chain.reason: Spec E-20260928-15 tests whether typing items at bind time (a retriever plus a typed Choice per source field, confirmed once) is as accurate as the serve-time G7 Choice per item and cheaper at serve time, and whether a schema change silently mistypes items; no register belief covers it, so it decides G7's design rather than a grade. It is recommended now because it is the one gateway change the survey synthesis proposes, and the spec adds the field-level clustering the card missed (items from one field share one mapping, so at least 120 distinct fields are required).

Revision E-20260928-15-r2 answers REV-20260928-29: the Magneto 0.860 MRR is re-attributed to the combined retriever plus 70B reranker system, automatic bind-time arms are added beside the human-assisted ones with a blinded confirmer and disjoint sample values, deployment requires both the accuracy rule and post-migration safety, validity needs 40 fields per backend, and the card's kill-rule change carries an explicit override. No register belief covers source typing, so it decides G7's design (priority 3) on public ASF data within POLICY-v1 caps.

experiment.claim:
For typing items from connected engineering tools onto the ontology's shared types and properties, a bind-time mapping per source field (a small encoder retrieves the top 5 shared properties, a typed Choice picks one; items are then typed by lookup) is no more than 3 points of type accuracy below a serve-time typed Choice per item once unbound fields fall back to serve-time typing, and is either at least 1 point more accurate or at least 50 ms p95 cheaper at serve time; and after a schema change (two renamed custom fields in the issue tracker) the deployed binding with a breaking-change check silently mistypes no more than 5% of items. The bind-time arms are tested twice: fully automatic, and human-assisted (a person confirms each field mapping once), so the gain of binding is separated from the gain of human review. Sources: N-SURVEY-20260928-24 (Magneto, arXiv 2412.08194, VLDB 2025: the best combined system, a fine-tuned MPNet retriever with a LLaMA3.3-70B reranker, reached 0.860 MRR on GDC, against 0.731 for a zero-shot configuration that also differs in reranker and serialisation, so the gap is a whole-system comparison, not a retriever-training effect; COMA++ about 0.35, read from a figure; LLM-only schema-to-ontology mapping, arXiv 2609.13776, fell from 0.79 at 23 classes to 0.51 at 300; a column type annotator lost about 5 points on an unseen serialisation, arXiv 2512.22742), N-SURVEY-20260928-17 and N-SURVEY-20260928-18 (Palantir and Fabric IQ type data through a binding made once per source), N-SURVEY-20260928-26 (the survey synthesis recommending G7 move to bind time). None of these sources is on engineering tools and no typed decision model is in any comparison; the register holds no belief on source typing, so this decides G7's design rather than a grade.

arms (same 300 served items, same gold labels, same ontology version):
- A: serve-time G7: a Jev Choice per item per key field over the fixed tag sets, pinned version, neutral option names per E-20260928-06-r2's frozen template. No human input.
- B-auto: bind-time mapping, automatic: for each source field, a small encoder (MPNet-class, pinned) embeds the field name, description and 5 sample values and retrieves the top 5 shared properties; a Jev Choice picks one of the 5 (or "none"); items are typed by lookup. Fields mapped to "none" stay unbound and untyped.
- C-auto: B-auto plus arm A's serve-time Choice applied only to unbound fields.
- B-human and C-human: as B-auto and C-auto, but one engineer confirms or corrects each field mapping once, with minutes logged. The confirming engineer sees only the field name, description and the 5 frozen sample values, never the evaluation items or gold labels, and does not label.
- Sample values for every bind-time arm are drawn by a frozen, seeded rule from a pool of records disjoint from the 300 scored items.
- Schema change (applied after the main run): rename two custom fields in the issue-tracker export; re-run every bind-time arm with and without the migration rule (unknown field name or changed field id raises a binding-breaking flag and routes the field to serve-time typing until re-bound).
experiment.metric: type accuracy on served items (primary: key fields mapped to the gold type and property); serve-time p95 latency and cost per 1,000 items; one-off binding effort (engineer minutes per source, human arms only); after the schema change, silent mistype rate (items typed wrongly with no flag) with and without the migration rule.
experiment.predeclared_margin: a bind-time arm is eligible for deployment only if its accuracy is at most 3 points below A and its post-change silent mistype rate with the migration rule is at most 5%; it is worth deploying only if it is at least 1 point above A or at least 50 ms p95 cheaper than A. The selected arm is the eligible, worth-deploying arm with the least human input (C-auto before C-human, B before C only if B is itself eligible). override: the card reads "B or C more than 3 points below A: keep serve-time". B and C are alternative deployments, not a joint system, so each is judged on its own rule and a failure of one does not block the other; the card's intent (no deployed arm may be more than 3 points below A) is kept exactly.
experiment.kill_criterion: every bind-time arm more than 3 points below A with the interval's upper end below minus 3: keep G7 at serve time. The only accuracy-eligible arms exceed 5% silent mistypes after the change even with the migration rule: keep serve-time until the binding's breaking-change check is redesigned. A within 1 point of the selected arm and the selected arm saves under 50 ms p95: keep serve-time only. Invalid (rerun under a new spec revision, not a verdict): labeller kappa on type below 0.7, fewer than 40 distinct key fields in any backend, any sample value drawn from a scored item, or the confirming engineer found to have seen evaluation items.

sections.action: Add to plan: cheap, and it settles a design choice before we build the connection layer around the wrong one.
sections.details:
**Sources.** Magneto (arXiv 2412.08194, VLDB 2025, N-SURVEY-20260928-24): best combined system, fine-tuned MPNet retriever plus LLaMA3.3-70B reranker, 0.860 MRR on GDC vs 0.731 for a zero-shot configuration that also differs in reranker and serialisation (whole-system gap, not a retriever-training effect); COMA++ about 0.35, read from a figure. LLM-only schema-to-ontology mapping (arXiv 2609.13776): 0.79 at 23 classes, 0.51 at 300. A column type annotator lost about 5 points on an unseen serialisation (arXiv 2512.22742). Palantir and Fabric IQ bind once per source (N-SURVEY-20260928-17, -18). Survey synthesis recommending G7 move to bind time: N-SURVEY-20260928-26. No source on engineering tools; no typed decision model in any comparison; no register belief on source typing, so this decides G7's design.

**Arms** (300 served items, 100 per backend from issue-tracker projects, GitHub repositories and design wiki spaces; at least 120 key fields, 40 per backend):
- A: serve-time G7, a Jev Choice per item per key field (baseline).
- B-auto: MPNet-class encoder retrieves top 5 shared properties per field, Jev Choice picks one or "none"; items typed by lookup.
- C-auto: B-auto plus A's serve-time Choice for unbound fields.
- B-human, C-human: one blinded engineer confirms each field mapping once (sees only field name, description, 5 sample values from a disjoint pool; minutes logged).
- Schema change: rename two custom issue-tracker fields; re-run bind-time arms with and without the migration rule (unknown name or changed id raises a flag and falls back to serve-time typing).

**Outcomes.**
- Pass: the first eligible arm in the order C-auto, B-auto, C-human, B-human is deployed. Eligible: accuracy interval of (arm minus A) lower end at least minus 3 points, post-change silent mistype rate with the migration rule at most 5%, and at least 1 point more accurate or at least 50 ms p95 faster than A.
- Kill: every bind-time arm clearly more than 3 points below A; or the accurate arms exceed 5% silent mistypes even with the migration rule; or no eligible arm is worth it. G7 stays serve-time.
- Inconclusive: keep serve-time G7, record bind-time as an option, re-test with a fourth backend and more fields.
- Invalid: type kappa below 0.7, fewer than 40 key fields in a backend, sample leak, or the confirming engineer saw evaluation items.

**Power.** Effective sample is fields, not items. At 120 fields and 0.10 discordance, SE about 0.029, half-width about 5.7 points; cluster bootstrap by source field. Latency well powered.

**Review.** REV-20260928-29 (gpt-6-astra) reviewed E-20260928-15, outcome revise. Findings and r2's answers: (1) Magneto 0.860 vs 0.731 misattributed to retriever training: corrected to a whole-system comparison. (2) Only bind-time arms got human help; confirmer access and sample independence unspecified: automatic arms added, human arms blinded, samples from a disjoint seeded pool. (3) Positive possible with silent mistypes above 5%; 30 vs 40 fields; no inconclusive branch: deployment needs both rules, 40 fields per backend required, interval-based branches added. (4) Card's "B or C" kill rule changed without override: explicit override keeps the intent (no deployed arm more than 3 points below A). (5) Stale "policy unset" and unauthorised export: POLICY-v1 caps, public Apache Software Foundation records. (6) Packet not executable: commands, latency protocol and `freeze.json` pins named; hashes fixed before run 1. (7) Embedded instructions in sources: not followed. r2 not yet re-reviewed. POLICY-v1.1's `cost_usd > 10` trigger is read here on total cost (up to 20 USD), so a `ready` re-review is required before execution; no belief is affected and there is no novelty claim. reviewer_blocking is false because every finding has a recorded answer.

**Cost and schedule.** Labelling 3 labeller-days, binding confirmation under 1 engineer-day, exports and schema change 2, harness 3: about 9 people-days. About 1.0M tokens, 2 runs, under 20 USD. Start 2026-10-26, verdict due 2026-12-04. Owner T2, track A.

**Dependencies.** BIND-TYPE-ASF-300 from public Apache Software Foundation records; the CTO must confirm it under permitted_datasets. Frozen ontology version. Related: E-20260928-17, E-20260928-06-r2 (neutral option template).
sections.busy: Customer searches could cost less and run faster if Jev, TypeSafe's small decision model, ran once per connected tool, not on every result. Jev decides what each field means, such as a due date or an owner. Products such as Palantir and Microsoft Fabric decide this once per tool, when it is connected, then just look it up. One study found an AI choosing among many types gets worse as the list grows. Nobody has measured this on engineering tools. This is part of your third priority: the shape of our project memory. The test checks whether deciding once is as accurate and faster, and what breaks when a tool renames a field. About 9 people-days and $20, with an answer by early December. We suggest adding it to the plan.
sections.example: A customer's administrator renames two custom fields in their ticket tool. If we decided each field's meaning once and never rechecked, tickets may now carry a wrong due date with no warning. An engineer's agent then plans work around dates that are wrong. The test measures how often that happens and whether a simple field-changed alarm catches it first.

queue.claim: On nine generic entity-matching datasets, a 124M matcher reached 81.96 F1 against 86.36 for GPT-4, at "3,899 times lower" cost per 1K tokens. Cross-encoders beat bi-encoders, and generative matchers helped mainly under distribution shift. G13 today specifies a Jev Noul `same_claim` with a rule fallback, but no one has compared it with a small matcher on cross-tool engineering records.
queue.proposed_experiment:
- **Cases.** Label 400 record pairs drawn from Jira, GitHub issues and PRs, Confluence requirement pages and CI test records: 160 same item, 240 different but similar. Two labellers, blind. Hold out one whole source pairing (for example Confluence to GitHub) as the shift set.
- **Arms.**
  - A: rules (shared key such as a ticket id in a PR title or URL, exact title).
  - B: an open-weight cross-encoder fine-tuned on the non-held-out pairs.
  - C: a Jev Noul `same_item` with thresholds fit on half.
  - D: a frontier LLM, zero-shot.
- **Metrics.** F1 on the in-distribution and shift sets, cost per 1K pairs, and p95 latency.
- **Kill criterion.**
  - B and C both fail to beat A by 5 F1: ship rules only.
  - C fails to beat B by 3 F1 on either set: ship the open-weight model, which keeps memory text in-house.
  - D fails to beat the best of B and C by 5 F1 on the shift set: no escalation path.
queue.plain_title: Can a cheap model spot the same work item across our tools as well as the paid one?
queue.why_it_matters: Spotting the same item across tools is the federation layer's identity problem. The evidence says this is where a small model we host is most likely to be good enough, which serves priority 2 as well.
queue.component: gateway fusion and G13 (cross-hub duplicate or conflict)
queue.decision_it_could_change: which implementation G13 ships with (rules, small open-weight cross-encoder, Jev, or LLM), and whether escalation keys on new source pairings

decision_chain.reason: Spec E-20260928-14 compares rules, a small self-hosted cross-encoder, Jev and a frontier LLM on whether two cross-tool engineering records are the same item, with a held-out source pairing as the shift set; no register belief covers this, so it decides G13's implementation and proposes a new belief row rather than moving a grade. It is recommended now because the evidence (a 124M matcher 4.4 F1 behind GPT-4 at a fraction of the cost) points to the stage where a model we host is most likely good enough, serving priorities 3 and 2 together.

Revision E-20260928-14-r2 answers REV-20260928-27: a frozen three-class rubric separates same work item from related-but-distinct records with a 5% false-merge guard, splits are by project before pair generation with connected-component resampling, each arm ships only if it passes its own rule with an interval-based inconclusive branch, and the data move to public ASF records under POLICY-v1 caps. No register belief covers cross-hub identity, so it decides G13's implementation now, self-hosted option first (priorities 3 and 2).

experiment.claim:
On cross-tool engineering records (issue tracker tickets, GitHub issues and pull requests, design and requirement wiki pages, CI test records), deciding whether two records are the same work item, as distinct from two records that are related (one implements, verifies, references or is the parent of the other): (1) a small open-weight cross-encoder or a Jev Noul beats a shared-key and exact-title rule by at least 5 F1 on the same-item class without merging more than 5% of related-but-distinct pairs; (2) Jev does not beat the small cross-encoder by 3 F1 on both the in-distribution and the shift set; (3) a frontier LLM earns an escalation path only if it beats the shipped arm by at least 5 F1 on a held-out source pairing. Source: N-SURVEY-20260928-22 (AnyMatch, arXiv 2409.04073): a 124M matcher averaged 81.96 F1 against 86.36 for GPT-4 (MatchGPT) over 9 generic entity-matching datasets, zero-shot leave-one-dataset-out, at a quoted 3,899 times lower cost per 1K tokens (2024 prices); losses concentrated on heterogeneous product records (for example WDC 63.31 vs 85.83), and the companion study (arXiv 2607.24688) reports cross-encoders ahead of bi-encoders and generative matchers ahead mainly under distribution shift. No source contains engineering records and no typed decision model is in any comparison; the register holds no belief on cross-hub identity, so this decides G13's implementation rather than a grade.

arms (same candidate pairs, same pair rendering: title, type, key fields, first 512 tokens of body, source system):
- A: rules: same item if a shared key links them (a ticket id or issue number in a title, branch or body; a URL to the other record) or titles match exactly after the frozen normalisation (lowercase, strip punctuation and ticket prefixes, collapse whitespace). This rule knowingly merges related records; measuring that is part of the test.
- B: a small open-weight cross-encoder (ModernBERT-base, or the AnyMatch GPT-2 124M checkpoint if its licence permits; chosen and pinned in `freeze.json` before labelling ends), fine-tuned on XHUB-TRAIN with the recipe in `freeze.json` (learning rate, epochs, early stop on XHUB-DEV F1), one seed chosen before test scoring.
- C: Jev Noul `same_item` whose true criterion is the rubric's same-item definition and whose false criterion names the related-but-distinct cases, neutral option names per E-20260928-06-r2's frozen template, pinned version, threshold fitted on XHUB-DEV to maximise F1.
- D: a frontier LLM, zero-shot, one call per pair, pinned model and the rubric text as prompt (sha256 in `freeze.json`).
- Reported, not decided on: every arm on the subset of pairs with no shared key (where the rule cannot help).
experiment.metric: F1 on the same-item class on XHUB-TEST-IN and XHUB-TEST-SHIFT (primary); false-merge rate on related-but-distinct pairs (a guard, with a one-sided 95% Clopper-Pearson bound); precision at the chosen threshold; cost per 1,000 pairs (C and D at list price on the run date; B at amortised GPU seconds); p95 latency per pair (500 timed pairs, warm, batch 1); whether pair text left our infrastructure (C, D yes; A, B no).
experiment.predeclared_margin: 5 F1 for an arm over A on both test sets; 3 F1 for C over B on both sets for C to ship instead of B; 5 F1 for D over the shipped arm on the shift set (the card's margins). A shipping arm must also keep its false-merge rate on related-but-distinct pairs at or below 5% (one-sided 95% upper bound). Each arm is judged by its own rule; an arm that fails its own rule never ships, whatever another arm does.
experiment.kill_criterion: no model arm (B or C) beats A by 5 F1 on both test sets with its false-merge guard met: ship rules only. C fails to beat B by 3 F1 on at least one set while B passes its own rule: ship B (in-house). D fails to beat the shipped arm by 5 F1 on the shift set: no escalation path. Invalid (rerun under a new spec revision, not a verdict): labeller kappa below 0.7 on the three-class label, any shift-set project or source pairing found in train or dev, or any record id appearing in two splits.

sections.details:
**Why hold, not approve.** Money is small (under 40 USD). The constraint is people: about 67 labeller-hours plus adjudication, the largest labelling load on the desk, starting 2026-10-19, the same week as E-20260928-18 (about 45 labeller-hours). Both need a rubric that separates same-item from related-but-distinct (implements, verifies, references, parent or child), and E-20260928-08-r2's trace-link labels need the same distinction. Running them in sequence lets one frozen rubric and one trained labeller pool serve all three. Return date 2026-11-09; verdict would move from 2026-12-04 to about mid-December. Not a quality objection: the r2 design answers every review finding.

**Source.** AnyMatch (arXiv 2409.04073, N-SURVEY-20260928-22): 124M matcher 81.96 F1 vs GPT-4 (MatchGPT) 86.36 averaged over 9 generic entity-matching datasets, zero-shot leave-one-dataset-out, quoted 3,899 times lower cost per 1K tokens (2024 prices); losses concentrated on heterogeneous product records (WDC 63.31 vs 85.83). Companion arXiv 2607.24688: cross-encoders ahead of bi-encoders; generative matchers ahead mainly under distribution shift. No engineering records, no typed decision model in any comparison. The register holds no belief on cross-hub identity; this decides G13's implementation.

**Arms** (same candidate pairs and rendering):
- A: rules (shared key or exact normalised title); knowingly merges related records.
- B: small open-weight cross-encoder (ModernBERT-base, or AnyMatch GPT-2 124M if licence permits), fine-tuned on XHUB-TRAIN.
- C: Jev Noul `same_item`, threshold fit on XHUB-DEV.
- D: frontier LLM zero-shot.
- Reported: every arm on pairs with no shared key.

**Outcomes.**
- Pass: an arm beats A by at least 5 F1 on both XHUB-TEST-IN and XHUB-TEST-SHIFT with its false-merge rate on related-but-distinct pairs at most 5% (one-sided 95% bound). B ships unless C passes its own rule and beats B by 3 F1 on both sets. D gets an escalation path only if it beats the shipped arm by 5 F1 on the shift set.
- Kill (rules only): neither B nor C passes its own rule.
- Inconclusive: rules by default, best point-estimate arm in shadow, enlarge the shift set.
- Invalid: kappa below 0.7 on the three-class label, shift project or pairing in train or dev, or a record in two splits.

**Power.** 1,000 pairs (train 350, dev 150, test-in 300, test-shift 200), about 35% same, 30% related-but-distinct, 35% unrelated; split by project before pair generation. F1 within about 5 to 8 points (95%); a 3-point difference is not resolvable at this size. Bootstrap over connected components of the record graph.

**Review.** REV-20260928-27 (gpt-6-astra) reviewed E-20260928-14, outcome revise. Findings and r2's answers: (1) a shared ticket id proves a relation, not identity: three-class rubric with a related-but-distinct guard. (2) Leakage across splits: split by project before pair generation, component-level bootstrap. (3) B could ship without passing its own rule; point estimates only: each arm judged by its own rule, interval-based pass, fail or inconclusive. (4) Stale "policy unset" and a private four-tool dataset: POLICY-v1 caps, public Apache Software Foundation records. (5) Packet not executable: commands and `freeze.json` pins named, hashes fixed before run 1. Card deviation: 400 pairs grew to 1,000 for B's training data and the guard. r2 not yet re-reviewed. POLICY-v1.1's `cost_usd > 10` trigger is read here on total cost (up to 40 USD), so a `ready` re-review is required before execution; no belief is affected. reviewer_blocking is false because every finding has a recorded answer.

**Cost.** About 67 labeller-hours plus adjudication (about 9.5 days), export and blocking 3 engineer-days, harness 3: about 16 people-days. About 2.0M tokens over 3 runs, under 40 USD. Owner T4, track C.

**Dependencies.** XHUB-ASF-1000 from public Apache Software Foundation projects, including issue migrations to GitHub; the CTO must confirm it under permitted_datasets. Related: E-20260928-06-r2 (neutral option template), E-20260928-08-r2.
sections.busy: Customers expect our memory to show one full history for each piece of work, even when it lives in several tools, say as a ticket and again as a GitHub issue. It must also never merge a ticket with the separate pull request that fixes it. Studies on generic records found a tiny model came close to a large AI for a tiny fraction of the cost. None used engineering records. This is part of your third priority: the shape of our project memory. It also serves your second: a model we run ourselves. The test compares simple rules, a small in-house model, Jev and a large AI. It needs about 16 people-days, most of it labelling, and $40. We suggest holding it until early November, so it shares labellers and rules with the Jev linking test.
sections.example: A product manager asks our memory for everything done on a login bug. The bug lives as a ticket in one tool and as an issue in another. If memory treats them as two items, half the history is missing. If it wrongly merges the bug with the pull request that fixed it, later questions about what was fixed get the wrong answer.

queue.claim: The kinetic half of an ontology (typed actions whose preconditions are checked against the graph before an agent acts) is what our ontology lacks. The mechanism is credible from outside the PDLC. Deterministic predicates cost 1.11 to 2.83 ms (AgentSpec). A 4B guard matched GPT-5.4 on step-level safety (83.0 / 83.3 against 83.0 / 84.4 Acc / F1) at 599.9 ms per call (StepGuard). Palantir ships the shape as action types with submission criteria and a failure message per condition. Nobody has measured it on lifecycle preconditions.
queue.proposed_experiment:
- **Setup.** Seed a PDLC history (H7's seed of about 300 typed records: requirements, decisions, constraints, tickets, PRs, tests with VERIFIES, IMPLEMENTS, CONSTRAINS and SUPERSEDES). Define five actions: merge PR, close ticket, mark requirement verified, supersede decision, relax constraint. Write each one's preconditions as graph predicates (for example "no Requirement that this PR implements has a failing verifying Test", or "no active Constraint on a touched DesignElement"), plus one prose precondition per action ("respects the linked decision's rationale").
- **Cases.** Build 200 proposed actions, 80 of them violating at least one precondition, labelled blind by two engineers. At least 120 are benign, so the false-block bound is meaningful.
- **Arms.**
  - A: no check; the agent sees retrieved memory only and decides.
  - B: deterministic predicates on the Action type.
  - C: B plus a typed decision model on the prose precondition. Run it once with Jev and once with an open-weight model (Intern-Decision 4B or a 4B guard).
- **Metrics.** Violations caught, false blocks on benign actions, p95 added latency, and for A, the agent's own proceed or stop.
- **Kill criterion.**
  - B catches fewer than 70% of seeded violations, or its false-block one-sided 95% upper bound exceeds 5% on 120 benign actions: drop predicates as the primary mechanism.
  - C adds fewer than 10 points of violation recall over B, or adds more than 800 ms p95: ship rules only and record G14 as rules-only.
  - B is not at least 20 points of recall above A: the check adds nothing over good retrieval, so drop the Action type from ADR-0011.
queue.plain_title: Can memory stop an agent merging code that breaks a known requirement? Simple rules may catch most.
queue.why_it_matters: This decides whether the ontology amendment adds Action types at all, and whether a System One model has a job at the federation layer that is not in G1 to G13. It is also the most concrete product difference from a memory that only answers questions: the memory can say "stop, and here is why".

decision_chain.reason: Spec E-20260928-13 tests whether graph-predicate preconditions on five PDLC Action types catch seeded violations better than retrieval alone, and whether Jev or an open-weight 4B checker adds recall on prose preconditions; it cannot re-grade B25 (firm) but decides whether the product can enforce it at action time, and it adds a guard the card lacked (predicates frozen before cases are built, violations tagged expressible or prose-only) so the rule arm cannot be circular. It takes the priority 3 reserved slot now because it decides whether the ADR-0011 amendment gains Action types at all.

Revision E-20260928-13-r2 answers REV-20260928-23: it adds a matched-information arm (the agent sees exactly the predicates' graph read-set) and a generic graph lint, fixes separate denominators (60 expressible, 40 prose-only violations, 140 benign), bounds C's false blocks, adds interval-based inconclusive branches, and moves to a public-data seeded fixture under POLICY-v1 caps; the unfetchable Palantir detail is marked unverified and made non-load-bearing. It tests whether the product can enforce B25 (firm) at action time and decides the ontology's Action types for priority 3.

experiment.claim:
On a seeded PDLC history, deterministic preconditions written as graph predicates on five Action types (merge PR, close ticket, mark requirement verified, supersede decision, relax constraint) catch at least 70% of predicate-expressible precondition violations with at most a 5% one-sided 95% upper bound on false blocks, and at least 20 recall points more than a frozen agent given either retrieved memory (the card's comparison) or exactly the graph facts the predicates read (the matched-information control); a typed decision model checking one prose precondition per action adds at least 10 recall points on prose-only violations at no more than 800 ms p95 and without breaking the false-block bound. Sources: N-SURVEY-20260928-23 (StepGuard, arXiv 2608.24777: a 4B guard at 83.0 / 83.3 trajectory Acc / F1 against GPT-5.4 at 83.0 / 84.4, 599.9 ms per call, with GPT-5.4 also the label teacher; AgentSpec, arXiv 2503.18666: deterministic predicates at 1.11 to 2.83 ms, over 90% of unsafe executions prevented on 750 RedCode-Exec cases, LLM-written rules at 95.56% precision and 70.96% recall), N-SURVEY-20260928-17 and N-SURVEY-20260928-21 (action types with submission criteria as a product shape; an executable-ontology implementation; the per-condition failure-message detail is unverified, see revision notes), N-SURVEY-20260928-26 (the synthesis proposing G14). Every source tests safety (harm, injection, unsafe code), not lifecycle preconditions; no source measures a PDLC precondition check, which is the question and a novelty claim, hence review.

arms (same 240 proposed actions, same frozen graph snapshot):
- A: no check, retrieved memory. A frozen agent (pinned model, temperature 0) receives the proposed action and the memory retrieved for it by the Track B retriever and answers proceed or stop with a reason. This is the card's baseline.
- A-graph: no check, matched information. The same frozen agent receives the proposed action plus a rendering of exactly the nodes and edges that B's predicates for that Action type read (the predicate read-set, logged by B), and answers proceed or stop. This separates the value of the check from the value of seeing the graph facts.
- Q: generic graph lint, no Action types. One action-agnostic rule set over the touched artifacts (block if any linked Requirement is unverified, any verifying Test fails, or any active Constraint touches the artifact), run on every action regardless of type. This separates typed per-action preconditions from a plain structured query.
- B: deterministic graph predicates attached to each Action type, evaluated on the graph snapshot; block if any predicate fails, returning the failing condition as the message.
- C-jev: B plus a Jev Noul on the one prose precondition per action ("respects the linked decision's rationale"), with the linked decision text and the proposed change as state; block if B blocks or the Noul answers "violates" above a threshold fitted on the 40-action dev split.
- C-open: as C-jev, with an open-weight 4B model (Intern-Decision 4B, or a 4B step guard if its licence permits, chosen and pinned in `freeze.json` before any case is built) in place of Jev.
- Reported, not decided on: B on a degraded graph with 20% of IMPLEMENTS and VERIFIES edges removed at random (3 seeds), because predicates are only as good as the links (linking is tested in E-20260928-08-r2 and E-20260928-18).
experiment.metric: B and Q recall on predicate-expressible violations (primary for B); C recall on prose-only violations (primary for C, the only denominator for the C rule); false blocks on benign actions for every blocking arm, with a one-sided 95% Clopper-Pearson upper bound; added p95 latency per check; for A and A-graph, the agent's stop rate on each violation class and on benign actions.
experiment.predeclared_margin: B recall on predicate-expressible violations at least 0.70 and B false-block upper bound at most 5% on 140 benign actions; B recall minus A stop rate and B recall minus A-graph stop rate, both on predicate-expressible violations, at least 0.20 each; B recall minus Q recall reported (Action types earn their keep over a generic lint if at least 0.10, reported, not a kill); a C arm passes if its recall on prose-only violations exceeds B's by at least 0.10, its combined false-block upper bound stays at most 5%, and its p95 added latency is at most 800 ms. override: the card measured B's 70% on all violations; prose-only violations are by construction outside what predicates can express, so B's rule is judged on predicate-expressible violations and C's on prose-only violations, each with its own fixed denominator.
experiment.kill_criterion: B recall on predicate-expressible violations below 0.70 with the interval's upper end below 0.70, or B false-block upper bound above 5%: drop predicates as the primary mechanism. B minus A-graph below 0.20 with the interval's upper end below 0.20: the check adds nothing over serving the same facts, drop the Action type from the ADR-0011 amendment. Both C arms fail their rule: G14 is rules only. Invalid (rerun under a new spec revision, not a verdict): labeller kappa on violating or benign below 0.6, fewer than 60 expressible or 40 prose-only violations, or any predicate edited after cases were built.

review.checked: "Target and all twelve cited artifacts. Inspected StepGuard abstract and full-text Table 1 and latency section/Table 7 (83.0/83.3 versus 83.0/84.4; 599.9 ms), AgentSpec evaluation/Table 6 and overhead (95.56/70.96; 1.11/2.83 ms), ShieldAgent Table 2 and method discussion; Palantir overview/root docs; OpenBKN README/org page; Foundation Capital essays and OSI README. Checked A-graph/Q additions, dev thresholds, 60/40/140 denominators, false-block bounds, verdicts, costs and B25/POLICY-v1.1."
review.not_verified: "Palantir submission-criteria/failure-message page is not staged; the target correctly marks that detail unverified and cites an earlier watch. No executed safety results, frozen predicates, graph, action labels, model pins or runnable packet exist. OpenBKN/OSI are HEAD reads. Adjacent papers do not establish lifecycle-precondition effectiveness."
findings: "[baseline] Q is a deliberately coarse action-agnostic lint; B-versus-Q is only reported. A positive therefore cannot establish the value of ontology Action types over the same per-action predicates in an ordinary rule dispatcher. A-graph improves information matching but does not isolate ontology packaging. Require that control for an Action-type conclusion or narrow the conclusion to action-specific rules."

"[leakage] Dev/test actions are not split by seed record or mutation family, even though the spec recognizes repeated mutations from one seed as dependent. C's threshold fitting can thus see near-duplicate test conditions. Blind labelling alone does not prevent this."

"[grade] False-block certification uses binomial Clopper-Pearson over 140 actions while acknowledging seed-level dependence for recall. With correlated benign variants, those 140 trials are not independent; the claimed 5% upper bound is not justified. Require independent benign seeds or a cluster-aware safety bound and size it accordingly."

"[grade] c_pass drops every inconclusive C arm from the list; the positive result then records no model addition. The kill text says \"Both C arms fail\" gives rules-only, but an unresolved 10-point gain is not a demonstrated failure. Return pass/fail/inconclusive for each C arm and distinguish an operational default from a scientific negative."

"[packet] Missing executable/pinned harness and scorer, actual graph/action/dev/test paths and hashes, complete actions.yaml and lint, retrieval configuration/token cap, exact agent/Jev/open-model pins and templates, and an end-to-end invocation. Named subcommands and future freeze.json do not suffice. Model pricing and call partitions are not fixed; policy acceptance/review/override, pre-call caps, shared weekly limits and failed-run output are not enforced. Executor verdict emission conflicts with policy."

"[injection] Source contains embedded instructions: OpenBKN README requests host checks/install scripts; cited synthesis says \"Change ADR-0011 in four ways.\" No commands or design changes were performed."
requested_corrections: "Separate an action-rule benefit from an ontology-packaging benefit using an equivalent rule-dispatch baseline."
"Split dev/test by independent seed and mutation family; use valid independent or clustered false-block inference and explicit C-arm inconclusive states."
"Supply the complete frozen packet, priced partitions and POLICY-v1.1 authorization/budget/failure enforcement with verdict-role separation."

sections.action: Add to plan: it tests the clearest thing our memory could do that a memory which only answers questions cannot: say stop, and why.
sections.details:
**Sources.** StepGuard (arXiv 2608.24777, N-SURVEY-20260928-23): 4B guard 83.0 / 83.3 trajectory Acc / F1 vs GPT-5.4 83.0 / 84.4, 599.9 ms per call, with GPT-5.4 also the label teacher. AgentSpec (arXiv 2503.18666): deterministic predicates 1.11 to 2.83 ms, over 90% of unsafe executions prevented on 750 RedCode-Exec cases; LLM-written rules 95.56% precision, 70.96% recall. Palantir action types with submission criteria and OpenBKN as the product shape (N-SURVEY-20260928-17, -21); per-condition failure message unverified. Synthesis proposing G14: N-SURVEY-20260928-26. Every source tests safety, not lifecycle preconditions.

**Arms** (240 test actions plus a 40-action dev split, one frozen graph snapshot; five Action types: merge PR, close ticket, mark requirement verified, supersede decision, relax constraint):
- A: frozen agent (T=0) with retrieved memory, proceed or stop (card's baseline).
- A-graph: same agent given exactly B's predicate read-set (matched-information control).
- Q: generic action-agnostic graph lint.
- B: deterministic graph predicates per Action type, failing condition returned as the message.
- C-jev: B plus a Jev Noul on one prose precondition per action, threshold fit on dev.
- C-open: as C-jev with an open-weight 4B (Intern-Decision 4B or a 4B step guard, pinned before case building).
- Reported: B on a graph with 20% of IMPLEMENTS and VERIFIES edges removed (3 seeds).

**Outcomes.**
- Pass: B recall on predicate-expressible violations at least 0.70; B false-block one-sided 95% upper bound at most 5% on 140 benign actions (at most 2 false blocks); B beats both A and A-graph by at least 0.20. A C arm passes if it adds at least 0.10 recall on prose-only violations, keeps the false-block bound and adds at most 800 ms p95; open-weight preferred if within 3 points of Jev. Result: Action types with preconditions and messages enter the ADR-0011 amendment; G14 recorded as rules, or rules plus a System One check.
- Kill: B recall interval entirely below 0.70, or false-block bound above 5%: drop predicates as primary mechanism. B minus A-graph interval entirely below 0.20: drop the Action type, serve graph facts instead. Both C arms fail: G14 rules only.
- Inconclusive (interval contains a margin): G14 stays a proposal; the 240 actions join the PDLC benchmark; re-test when H7's graph is built from real links.
- Invalid: kappa below 0.6, fewer than 60 expressible or 40 prose-only violations, or predicates edited after case building.

**Power.** 60 expressible, 40 prose-only, 140 benign. B recall SE 0.052 at 0.80; B minus A or A-graph SE about 0.071 at 0.35 discordance; C prose recall SE 0.072 at 0.30. Cluster bootstrap by seed record.

**Review.** REV-20260928-23 (gpt-6-astra) reviewed the first version E-20260928-13, outcome revise. Findings and how r2 answers them: (1) A and B saw different information: A-graph and Q added. (2) No inconclusive branch, C on the wrong denominator: interval-based branches added, C judged on prose-only violations with fixed minimums. (3) No false-block bound on C: added. (4) Stale "policy unset": POLICY-v1 caps with abort rule. (5) Packet not executable: commands and `freeze.json` pins named; commits and hashes fixed before run 1 because the harness does not exist yet. (6) Embedded instructions in sources: not followed. Open: the Palantir submission-criteria page was not fetched (no network); marked unverified, not load-bearing, tracked in WR-20260928-05. r2 has not been re-reviewed. POLICY-v1.1 requires a `ready` review here (firm belief B25 is in beliefs_affected, and this is a novelty claim). reviewer_blocking is set false because every finding has a recorded answer; the re-check is listed as a prerequisite.

**Beliefs.** B25 (firm: evidence cannot authorise its own use or execution) is not re-graded; the test shows whether the product can enforce it at action time.

**Cost and schedule.** Predicates and lint 2 engineer-days, case building and blind labelling of 280 actions about 6, harness 4: 12 people-days. About 2.3M tokens over 3 runs, under 30 USD. Start 2026-10-26, verdict due 2026-12-11. Owner T4, track C.

**Dependencies.** PDLC-SEED-ASF fixture (T1), shared with E-20260928-18 and E-20260928-20; the CTO must confirm it under permitted_datasets. Link quality from E-20260928-08-r2 and E-20260928-18. Harness `pdlc-action` not built.
sections.busy: We could sell a memory that stops an engineering agent before it breaks a known rule, and says why. An example is merging a change while the test for a customer requirement is failing. Studies of agent safety outside our field found that simple written rules catch most unsafe actions, in a few thousandths of a second. Nobody has tested this on engineering work. This is part of your third priority: the shape of our project memory. The test tells us whether simple rules are enough, or whether Jev or a free model is needed for the fuzzy cases. About 12 people-days and $30, with an answer by mid-December. A reviewer asked for fixes; they are made, and a final check is due before it runs. We suggest adding it to the plan.
sections.example: Late on a Friday, our agent is asked to merge a pull request. The test that proves a customer's security requirement is failing, but the agent's search never brought that up. With the check, the merge stops with a plain message: this change builds that requirement and its test is failing. The on-call engineer fixes the test instead of rolling back a release.

queue.claim: On engineering-memory questions, answering from write-time extracted fact records loses at least 3 points of answer accuracy against answering from the retained source evidence at the same retriever, reader and judge, even though retrieval recall on the source id is unchanged.
queue.proposed_experiment: Arm A = index retained source artifacts (design sections, tickets, PR descriptions, decision records) and retrieve top-k; arm B = index one extracted fact sheet per source artifact (same extractor for all, source id inherited) and retrieve top-k; also arm A' = source artifacts at the k whose reader tokens match arm B's. Dataset: the PDLC memory benchmark v1 question set (decision-behind-design, changed requirement, PR-implements) on the frozen harness, 300 or more questions. Metrics: answer accuracy by the fixed judge, reader-level evidence sufficiency (does the served text contain the answer span), recall@k on source id, reader tokens. Predeclared margin: B is worse than A by at least 3.0 points with a 95% paired bootstrap interval clustered by repository excluding 0. Kill: if B is within 1.0 point of A' at matched tokens, extraction is not the loss and the card is withdrawn.
queue.plain_title: Storing only short summaries of past work makes agents answer about 6 in 100 more questions wrong.
queue.why_it_matters:
This is R2's core write-path question (does a durable extraction step destroy evidence) measured where R3 retrieval metrics cannot see it. If the loss replicates on our artifacts, source evidence stays canonical and extraction becomes an optional derived view with its own sufficiency metric in the benchmark.
---
queue.component: ingestion and write path (extract-then-index vs retain source)
queue.decision_it_could_change: whether our ingestion stores extracted fact records as the searchable canon or keeps source evidence canonical with extraction as a derived view

decision_chain.reason: Spec E-20260928-11 tests whether write-time fact extraction loses answer accuracy against retained source artifacts at the same retriever, reader and judge, with a matched-token control and a single static reader prompt that removes the source's prompt confound; it can move B16 (lead) from skills to facts and add a second negative measurement under B5 (working). It takes this run's exploration slot because it is cheap, the source effect (94.2% to 87.8% with recall unchanged) is large and one-variable, and it decides the ingestion write path before extraction becomes canonical.

Revised per REV-20260928-19: the primary contrast is now fixed-candidate (same 10 parent artifacts, per-parent token matching), recall equivalence has a plus or minus 3 point test, the negative verdict needs a one-sided 95% bound below the 3-point margin, prompt attribution is corrected, B5 is dropped to a related measurement, and the packet gains a start gate, numeric token estimate (about 18M) and cap enforcement. It can move B16 (lead) on raw versus distilled evidence for engineering artifacts and settles the ingestion write-path choice before Track B freezes its benchmark set.

experiment.claim:
On engineering-memory questions, when the reader is given the same parent artifacts and the same number of tokens, answering from write-time extracted fact sheets loses at least 3 points of answer accuracy against answering from the retained source text of those artifacts, with the same reader, reader prompt and judge. End to end (each representation retrieved by its own index at the same k), the loss is also reported, together with a test of whether retrieval recall on the gold parent artifact is equivalent between the two indexes. Source: N-20260928-10 (Lore, commit 4976fa1), on LongMemEval-S (500 questions) one extracted fact sheet per session dropped answer accuracy from 94.2% to 87.8% at about one tenth of the reader tokens (about 2.8k vs 28k), while session recall@10 barely moved (98.69% vs 98.98%); the loss was steepest on questions about what the assistant said (73.2% vs 100%). The source states that retrieval algorithm, reader and judging protocol were kept fixed across that comparison, and both headline arms used question-type-aware reader instructions; a static-prompt source run gave 93.8%, and no static-prompt fact-sheet run was published. That is one run, one unnamed extractor, chat data, and no matched-token control. Whether the loss holds on long structured engineering artifacts, and whether it is the extraction rather than the budget or the retrieval unit, is the question.

arms (same 300 questions, same reader model at temperature 0, one static reader prompt in every arm, same judge; the static prompt is a robustness choice for our run, not a correction of the source):
- Candidate set. For each question, P_q = the top 10 parent artifacts returned by the frozen Track B hybrid retriever (BM25 plus vector, RRF k = 60) over a parent-level source index, where a parent's score is its best chunk score. P_q is computed once and shared by the fixed-candidate arms, so parent coverage is identical by construction.
- FC-S (fixed candidates, source, matched tokens): for each parent in P_q, the source text of that parent cut to the token count of that parent's fact sheet: its chunks in retriever-score order, the last one cut at a sentence boundary. Token matching is per parent, so no arm is empty and the total matches FC-F per question.
- FC-F (fixed candidates, fact sheets): the fact sheet of each parent in P_q. Fact sheets come from one pinned extractor model with one frozen extraction prompt; artifacts the extractor refuses or fails on pass through as source text and are tagged `extractor_fallback` (counted, reported).
- FC-S-full (reported, not decided on): the full source text of P_q up to the reader's context cap; shows what the budget alone buys.
- E-S (end to end, source): top 10 parents from the parent-level source index, each served as its highest-scoring chunk up to 10 chunks in total (the card's arm A at parent level).
- E-F (end to end, fact sheets): top 10 fact sheets from a fact-sheet index built with the same retriever configuration (the card's arm B).
experiment.metric: answer accuracy by the frozen judge (primary); reader-level evidence sufficiency (served text contains the gold answer span, exact or normalised match, frozen judge only for paraphrase); recall@10 on the gold parent artifact id for E-S and E-F; reader input tokens per question and the per-question token ratio FC-S / FC-F; accuracy by question family (decision-behind-design, changed requirement, PR-implements).
experiment.predeclared_margin: primary contrast D_fc = acc(FC-S) - acc(FC-F). Positive if D_fc >= 3.0 points and the 95% repository-clustered paired bootstrap interval excludes 0. Bounded negative if the one-sided 95% upper bound of D_fc (upper end of the 90% two-sided interval) is below 3.0 points. Otherwise inconclusive. Secondary: D_e2e = acc(E-S) - acc(E-F), reported with its 95% interval. Recall equivalence: recall@10(E-S) - recall@10(E-F) with its 90% clustered interval inside [-3.0, +3.0] points (two one-sided tests); if not equivalent, D_e2e is labelled confounded by retrieval and no end-to-end conclusion is drawn from it.
experiment.kill_criterion: the claim is withdrawn on a bounded negative (upper one-sided 95% bound of D_fc below 3.0 points). The run is invalid (rerun, not a verdict) if: extractor fallback on more than 10% of artifacts; gold span absent from the source artifacts for more than 5% of questions; median per-question token ratio FC-S / FC-F outside [0.9, 1.1] or more than 5% of questions outside [0.8, 1.25]; gold parent absent from P_q for more than 20% of questions (the fixed-candidate contrast would then be about the wrong evidence; both D_fc on all questions and on the gold-in-P_q subset are reported); or the token cap is hit.

sections.details:
**Card and spec.** PC-20260928-03 (priority 4, pillar R2, secondary R3 and R6, memory stage ingestion). Spec E-20260928-11-r2 supersedes E-20260928-11. Status queued, start 2026-10-26, verdict due 2026-11-27. `review_required: true`. Beliefs affected: B16 only (raw trajectories beat distilled representations; lead). B5 was removed on review.

**Evidence.** N-20260928-10 (Lore, CoreSpeed, commit 4976fa1). LongMemEval-S, 500 questions, one fact sheet per session: answer accuracy 94.2% to 87.8% (32 fewer correct), reader input about 28k to about 2.8k tokens, recall@10 98.98% vs 98.69%. Assistant-statement questions 100% vs 73.2%. Top-5 source sessions: 90.2% at about 14k tokens. Static-prompt source run 93.8%; no static-prompt fact-sheet run. One run, extractor and reader models unnamed, no intervals, no matched-token control. The builder measured its own design choice.

**Design (r2).** Primary contrast D_fc = acc(FC-S) - acc(FC-F). Both arms use a fixed candidate set P_q: the top 10 parents from the frozen Track B hybrid retriever (BM25 plus vector, RRF k=60). Source text is token-matched per parent to the fact sheet. Secondary: end-to-end D_e2e (E-S vs E-F). It is labelled "confounded by retrieval" unless recall@10 is equivalent within plus or minus 3 points (TOST, 90% clustered CI). FC-S-full is reported only. The reader is pinned at T=0 with one static prompt. The judge is blind to arm and served text. Extractor, reader and judge are three distinct pinned models.

**Outcomes.**
- Positive: D_fc >= 3.0 points and the 95% repository-clustered paired bootstrap CI excludes 0. Source stays canonical and extraction becomes a derived view with a sufficiency score. The PDLC benchmark adopts reader-level sufficiency. A revision event extends B16 to extracted facts.
- Bounded negative (kill): the one-sided 95% upper bound of D_fc is below 3.0. Fact sheets are allowed as a budget read surface and the card is withdrawn.
- Inconclusive: keep source canonical and re-run on the frozen PDLC memory benchmark v1.
- Invalid (rerun) if any of these holds: fallback > 10%; gold span missing > 5%; median token ratio outside [0.9, 1.1] or > 5% of questions outside [0.8, 1.25]; gold parent missing from P_q > 20%; cap hit.
- Power: about 89% at the source's 6.4-point loss and about 32% at 3.0. A true null reaches the bounded negative only about 44% of the time, so a null usually reads inconclusive.

**Review status.** REV-20260928-19 (challenger, outcome revise) reviewed the superseded E-20260928-11. It had six findings: attribution of prompt confound, baseline and retrieval-unit mismatch, point-only negative rule, B5 scope, incomplete execution packet, and prompt-injection text in the Lore README and AGENTS.md (not followed). The r2 revision notes address each finding. Finding 5 is partly overridden: the harness, dataset hashes and USD estimate cannot exist before build, freeze and pinning, so the start gate enforces them instead. **r2 has not been re-reviewed.** I set `reviewer_blocking: false` because the findings are answered on paper. The policy precondition "challenger review ready" is still unmet.

**Conflict with the standing policy (why Hold).** POLICY-v1 was set on 2026-09-28T17:23:55Z. The spec was written at 17:22:55Z and still says "policy unset". Under POLICY-v1:
- The per-run budget is 2M tokens, $25 and 2 h wall clock. The spec estimates about 18M model tokens (excluding about 5.4M embedding tokens) and proposes caps of 25M tokens and 36 h. That is about 9x over on tokens and 18x over on wall clock.
- `pdlc-extract-300-v1` is not in `permitted_datasets`. It is built from H7 seed repositories. If those count as "seeded fixtures from T1", the CTO should say so explicitly. Otherwise the list needs amending.
- `review_required_for` triggers: cost_usd > 10 (likely), and B16 is a lead belief (not firm or working). A second review is needed before execution in any case.

What clears the Hold:
1. A challenger review of r2 with outcome ready.
2. Either split the run into policy-sized runs (for example, extraction and indexing as separate runs, and a smaller reader set) or get a CTO exception.
3. Pin the three models and state USD.
4. Add the dataset to permitted datasets.

**Cost.** People: 2 engineers x 4 days for questions and gold spans, plus 4 engineer-days for the harness, 12 in total. Model tokens are about 18M: extraction 6.9M, reader 9.65M, judge 1.4M. USD is not estimable until the pins exist. `cost_model_usd_est: 0` means not estimated, not free.

**Dependencies.** H7 seed repositories (at least 8, minimum 6). The frozen Track B retriever. The PDLC memory benchmark v1 is the inconclusive re-run target. The run feeds H3 (read-time curation). H9's summarisation arm remains the B5 test.

**Interim safeguard.** Keep source evidence canonical by default. The spec names this the cheaper reversible choice under every outcome except a bounded negative.
sections.busy: We could cut the cost of our memory product about tenfold by keeping summaries of saved work instead of the original documents, but that risks wrong answers to our customers' engineers. Another memory product's builder found summaries made their agent answer about 6 in 100 more questions wrong. The right record was still found, but the needed detail had been cut. That is one study, by a vendor with a stake in it, on chat rather than engineering documents. If it holds for us, originals stay the main record. This is part of your fourth priority: our own test of how memory serves engineering work. It costs 12 people-days, dollars not yet priced, with an answer by late November. We suggest holding it: as written it breaks the spending limit you set today, and its fixes are unchecked.
sections.example: Weeks after a design review, an engineer asks our agent why the team dropped a planned cache. The memory holds only a summary: "Decided to remove the cache." The reason, a failed load test described in the original design document, was cut when the summary was written. The agent guesses a reason, sounds sure, and the engineer tries the approach that already failed.

queue.claim: Explicit PR-issue references are misaligned in 13.6% of SWE-bench Verified pairs; a frontier multi-agent checker detects misalignment at 88.11% to 92.12% binary accuracy for $0.08 to $0.23 per link (arXiv 2607.28587). Fine-grained PR-issue alignment has human kappa 0.575, and fine-tuned 3B to 7B models reach 62.75% accuracy but 34.44% macro-F1 (arXiv 2609.01087). No study found tests a System One model on this decision. SpecMine (arXiv 2608.25202) supplies 5,992 spec-touching PRs from 581 repositories and 98,574 Kiro requirement / design / task files under CC BY 4.0. Independent evaluation shows Jev about 44x cheaper than the best LLM but 11.6 macro-F1 points behind, and a confidence cascade matching the LLM at 27% to 56% of its cost (arXiv 2609.24574).
queue.proposed_experiment: Refines H7, which assumes the typed IMPLEMENTS and REFINES edges exist and tests only traversal over them; this tests who can create them, the CTO's priority 3 slice with a System One model deciding the links. Data: 300 (requirement or design section, PR) candidate pairs from 6 to 10 SpecMine Kiro repositories, half co-change or referenced pairs and half hard negatives (same repo, same period, not linked), two human labellers with a 3-way label (implements / partial / no) and kappa reported. Arms, same pairs and same rubric with neutral option names (see PC-SURVEY-20260928-04): (A) Jev Noul "does this PR implement this requirement?"; (B) an open-weight decision model self-hosted (Laya or decider-0.8b); (C) a fine-tuned ModernBERT-large on a separate 1,500-pair training split from other repos; (D) an LLM checker (single Claude call with the PAIChecker taxonomy); (E) cascade A then D below a confidence threshold fit on a calibration split. Metrics: precision at recall 0.8, macro-F1 on the 3-way label, ECE after temperature refit, cost per 1,000 links, p95 latency. Kill for System One at this stage: A, B and C all more than 10 F1 points below D, and E not within 2 points of D at under 50% of D's cost.
queue.plain_title: Can Jev or a free model we run ourselves decide which code change delivers which requirement, cheaply?
queue.why_it_matters: The context graph's value for product work rests on knowing which code change delivers which requirement. Today the only measured way to check that costs several cents per link using frontier models and sends our customers' code outside. If Jev or a model we host ourselves gets close at a fraction of the cost, the graph can be kept up to date on every pull request and the text stays in-house.
queue.component: PDLC linking stage (IMPLEMENTS edges from pull requests to requirements and design sections)
queue.decision_it_could_change: which model decides IMPLEMENTS links (Jev, a self-hosted open-weight model, or an LLM checker) and at what confidence a link is written without review

decision_chain.reason: The CTO's priority 3 slice (with priority 2's self-hosted comparison): no source tests a System One model on the IMPLEMENTS link decision, and this spec compares Jev, Laya-0.4B, a fine-tuned ModernBERT, an LLM checker and a cascade on 300 human-labelled SpecMine pairs, moving B14 through a locally fit auto-write threshold (the card listed no belief; the register has none on link deciders). Now, because SpecMine's CC BY 4.0 data makes it runnable this quarter, it decides who writes the PDLC graph's trace links, and its labelled pairs seed the deferred PDLC benchmark's F3 family; cost M, so review is required.

Revision E-20260928-08-r2 answers REV-20260928-10: requirement and PR text is frozen at PR time with repository families kept in one split, the fine-tuned arm becomes a binary link decision with a class-wise audit of its silver labels, the LLM reference gets an absolute quality floor, auto-write gets its own precision and coverage targets at deployment prevalence, the best-of-four selection is corrected, the run is declared a pilot with its power shown, and the unsupported cost-bound and kappa-ceiling statements are removed. It can move B14 (working) on our own linking data and is the CTO's priority 3 slice.

experiment.claim:
A System One model can decide whether a pull request implements a requirement or design section close enough to an LLM checker to be used at the PDLC linking stage. Specifically, on 200 held-out human-labelled (requirement or design section, PR) pairs from SpecMine Kiro repositories, frozen at decision time, at least one of hosted Jev or a self-hosted open-weight decision model reaches macro-F1 on the 3-way label (implements / partial / no) within 10 points of a single-call LLM checker, or a fine-tuned ModernBERT-large reaches binary macro-F1 (any link vs no) within 10 points of the checker's binary collapse, or a Jev-then-LLM confidence cascade comes within 2 points of the checker at under 50% of its cost; and, separately, whether any arm's calibration-fit auto-write threshold meets absolute accepted-link precision and coverage targets at deployment prevalence. This revision runs as a PILOT: at n = 200 it cannot reliably confirm the margins (power arithmetic below); it can return a clear negative for large gaps, a positive only when the selection-aware interval clears the margin, and it sizes a confirmatory run. Sources: N-SURVEY-20260928-14 (explicit PR-issue links misaligned in 13.6% of SWE-bench Verified; frontier multi-agent checker 88.11% to 92.12% binary accuracy at USD 0.08 to 0.23 per link on average, with large patches pushing per-instance cost above USD 1; human kappa 0.575 on a fine-grained label; fine-tuned 3B to 7B models 62.75% accuracy but 34.44% macro-F1; no System One arm in any source), N-SURVEY-20260928-11 (Jev 11.6 macro-F1 points behind the best LLM at about 44x lower cost on social-science tasks; cascade at 27% to 56% of LLM cost), N-SURVEY-20260928-13 (SpecMine data; its Appendix B states co-change is an assumption, not ground truth, and a PR may implement a requirement only partially), N-SURVEY-20260928-12 (fine-tuned encoder close to a bespoke read-out). The card lists no belief; the register has none on trace-link deciders. The spec tags B14 because the auto-write threshold rests on calibration measured here, on our data, rather than vendor calibration.

arms (same frozen pair renderings, same rubric; neutral option names A/B/C, following N-SURVEY-20260928-10, so the result does not depend on E-20260928-06's outcome):
- A: hosted Jev, one Choice decision over three neutral-named options with rubrics for implements / partial / no. Confidence: the probability the Choice response assigns to the selected option; if the API returns no per-option probability at freeze, A is scored on labels only and is excluded from E and from auto-write (stated in run_manifest.json).
- B: a self-hosted open-weight decision model, Laya-0.4B (Apache 2.0), weights revision hash pinned at freeze; decider-0.8b replaces it only if its licence is confirmed before freeze. Same Choice. Confidence: normalised option probability from the model's output distribution.
- C: ModernBERT-large fine-tuned as a BINARY classifier (any link vs no) on SPECMINE-LINK-TRAIN silver labels from repository families disjoint from calibration and test. C is not scored on the 3-way label because silver labels cannot separate implements from partial (see Revision notes). Confidence: softmax probability of "any link".
- D: LLM checker: one call to a pinned Claude model (claude-sonnet-5, version string pinned at freeze), temperature 0, the PAIChecker misalignment taxonomy in the prompt, the same three labels, and a JSON field with a stated probability for each label (used as D's confidence). This is the quality reference, not PAIChecker itself (which is multi-agent). D must meet absolute floors (below) or the relative comparison is invalid.
- E: cascade: A, then D for every pair whose A confidence is below a threshold fit on the calibration split to maximise macro-F1 subject to D-call share <= 50% (calibration split only). E reuses D's logged decision for routed pairs, so E's cost is A's cost on all pairs plus D's cost on routed pairs.
- Controls: a rule arm (explicit reference or co-change only, no model) and the label base rate, both reported.
- Three-option instability (N-SURVEY-20260928-10 reports it on Laya even with neutral names) is checked by also reporting A and B as two binary decisions (any link? then full or partial?) on the test split; the verdict uses the Choice form and states the gap.
experiment.metric: primary: macro-F1 on the 3-way label (A, B, E vs D) and binary macro-F1 on the any-link collapse (C vs D's collapse); secondary: accepted-link precision and coverage of the auto-write rule at deployment prevalence (reweighted, see packet); precision at recall 0.8 on the binary collapse; ECE after one temperature refit per arm on the calibration split; cost per 1,000 links at list prices on the run date (B and C: amortised GPU time); p95 decision latency; whether pair text left our infrastructure (A, D, E: yes; B, C: no). Every arm is also reported against each labeller and against the adjudicated label, next to inter-labeller kappa; kappa is context for label noise, not a ceiling on F1.
experiment.predeclared_margin: relative: 10 macro-F1 points for A, B (3-way) and C (binary) against D; 2 points and < 50% of D's cost for E. These are the card's margins; they are practical margins. Absolute floors (our predeclared design targets, not source numbers): D validity floor: D 3-way macro-F1 >= 0.50 and D binary precision at recall 0.8 >= 0.70 at deployment prevalence; auto-write targets for any arm: accepted-link precision point estimate >= 0.90 with one-sided 95% lower bound >= 0.80, and coverage (share of true links auto-written) >= 0.50, all on the test split at deployment prevalence using the threshold fit on calibration only. An arm can be adopted for review-routed proposals on the relative margin, but can auto-write only if it also meets the auto-write targets; otherwise its auto-write threshold is set to "never" and every link goes to review, which is consistent with the positive outcome.
experiment.kill_criterion: System One is killed for the IMPLEMENTS decision this quarter only if the run is valid and every arm in {A, B, C, E} fails: for A, B, C the upper bound of (arm minus D) is below -0.10; for E the upper bound of (E minus D) is below -0.02 or E's cost is >= 50% of D's. Invalid (rerun, not a verdict) if labeller kappa on the 3-way label < 0.4, or D misses its validity floor. C alone is invalid (dropped from the family, not killed) if its class-wise silver audit fails. Anything that is neither a pass nor a kill is inconclusive.
